title: KAS-8 — Render _kiro/system/notify {level, message} instead of dropping it
description:
KAS 0.17.2 (kiro-cli 2.12.3) adds connection-scoped notification _kiro/system/notify {level, message}, wired to the agent's onDelayMessage hook (system/delay messages, e.g. throttling or long-wait notices). Same family as cyril-3zy4 (_kiro/error/rate_limit) and cyril-3ald (_kiro/safety/*): a KAS-aware cyril should render these as system chat lines with level-appropriate styling, not silently drop. Note _kiro/system/ is a PREFIX namespace (CONNECTION_SCOPED_NOTIFICATION_PREFIXES = ['_kiro/sessions/', '_kiro/system/']) — handle unknown _kiro/system/* kinds gracefully. Reference: docs/kiro-2.12.3-wire-audit.md.

TRIGGER CONFIRMED (bundle read 2026-07-15): the onDelayMessage hook is fired by QClientRetryStrategy during model-request backoff — NOT remote/cloud-only. Two canned cases: delayMs>WARN threshold -> (DELAY_WARN_MESSAGE, level='warning'); delayMs>INFO threshold -> (DELAY_INFO_MESSAGE, level='info'). So level values seen = info|warning, messages are canned 'model is taking longer than usual'-type strings. Fires on ordinary slow/throttled LOCAL KAS turns, so any KAS-aware cyril will receive it in normal use — not an exotic remote path. Emit = connection.extNotification('_kiro/system/notify', {level, message}). New in KAS 0.17.2 (0 in 2.12.1).

notes.content: Closed: Shipped: PR #60 merged to main. KAS _kiro/system/notify {level, message} now renders as level-prefixed system message. 8 AC fences pass: converter (7), UI (2 includes busy-preservation). Fixed in-branch: simplified Unknown-level arm per bot review. Filed: none.

title: `--prompt` CLI option is parsed but never submitted
description: While smoke-testing cyril-6bol end to end, Cyril accepted `--prompt "run the requested smoke"`, created the session, and then remained idle. `crates/cyril/src/main.rs` defines `Cli::prompt` but has no read of `cli.prompt`; submitting the same text through the TUI immediately completed the terminal callback smoke. Wire the parsed one-shot prompt into startup without changing interactive startup behavior.
acceptance_criteria: A process started with `--prompt TEXT` submits TEXT once after the initial session is ready and the agent receives one `session/prompt`; without `--prompt`, startup remains interactive and submits nothing. Add an end-to-end fake-agent fence that fails when the option is parsed but unused.

notes.content: Closed: Fixed: PR #88 (af5ded2a6). Repro: oneshot_prompt_submitted_after_session_ready (red pre-fix, plus mutation check). One-shot rides the deferred-command path after first main SessionCreated; /new never replays; empty --prompt warns.

title: AgentProcess stderr piped but never drained — >64KB cumulative stderr wedges the agent; crash diagnostics discarded
description:
Found by the 2026-07-01 KAS implementation review. AgentProcess::spawn sets .stderr(Stdio::piped()) but child.stderr is never taken or read anywhere (transport.rs:25; verified by grep — _child just holds it). Once the child writes ~64KB (Linux pipe buffer) cumulatively to stderr, its next stderr write BLOCKS the whole process -> the engine wedges mid-turn with no error anywhere (and per cyril-l7tw, the wedge is silent).

Predates KAS but KAS makes it material: the engine is `node --experimental-wasm-modules` (Node emits runtime warnings to stderr by default) running an 801MB TypeScript agent whose logging/tracebacks go to stderr, over sessions that can run for hours. Even below the wedge threshold, everything KAS prints to stderr — including the reason for a spawn-then-immediate-crash — is discarded, so 'ACP initialization failed' is all the user ever gets.

Fix shape: take() stderr and spawn a drain task on the LocalSet (debug!-log lines; ring-buffer the tail so BridgeDisconnected reasons can include it — pairs with cyril-l7tw's visibility fix).
acceptance_criteria: An agent process writing >64KB to stderr does not stall (test with a chatty stub); drained stderr appears at debug level in cyril.log; the last N stderr lines are available to the disconnect path for actionable BridgeDisconnected reasons.

notes.content: Closed: Fixed: PR #41 (5185b2f + bce5472 bounded-read review fix). Repro: chatty_stderr_does_not_wedge_agent_process + newline_free_stderr_flood_drains_in_bounded_chunks; tail fences stderr_tail_keeps_only_last_n_lines / stderr_tail_snapshot_holds_final_lines_after_exit.

title: KAS: consume turn_completion summary + focus_update + _kiro/governance/state (currently all dropped)
description:
Systematic pass over the live KAS trace (experiments/conductor-spike/kas-live-session-trace-2.11.0.jsonl) found 3 agent->client message kinds cyril drops that carry genuinely useful UI signal:
1. session_info_update::turn_completion — {elapsedTime(ms), status(success|aborted), promptTurnSummaries:[{unit:'credit', unitPlural, usage(float), usedTools:[...]}]}. RICHER than cyril's flat MetadataUpdated metering (single credit number): per-turn cost + duration + the full list of tools the turn used (e.g. turn 2 = 22.17 credits, 769686ms, [user_input, invoke_sub_agent, grep_search, read_file, report_progress, subagent_response, ...]). Could power a per-turn cost/activity summary line. cyril's session_info_to_notification (kas.rs) handles only turn_end + context_usage; turn_completion falls to _ => None.
2. session_info_update::focus_update — {focus:{title}, title} = the agent's current focus ('Start a new spec called multiple-notes...'). A 'what it's working on' status-line indicator. Dropped.
3. _kiro/governance/state — {isEnterprise, features:{mcpEnabled, webToolsEnabled, usageAnalytics, contentCollection, promptLogging, codeReferenceTracker, autonomousAgents}}. Org/enterprise feature gating: which capabilities the org allows. Advisory (backend enforces) but a real UI-gating input (hide web-tools/MCP affordances when disabled, show content-collection indicator). Dropped.
All three drop safely today (no crash) — this is opt-in display work when the KAS converter (KAS-2/KAS-4) is fleshed out. STRUCTURAL NOTE: KAS session_info_update kinds double-encode (typed sub-object + flattened fields); read the flat _meta.kiro.X consistently. Full inventory in the trace companion doc.
acceptance_criteria: KAS converter maps turn_completion -> a per-turn summary notification (cost + usedTools + elapsed); focus_update -> a status indicator; _kiro/governance/state -> feature flags the UI can gate on. Each degrades gracefully (v2 has no equivalent). Reads the flat _meta.kiro.* encoding.

title: Bridge must reap KAS/kiro-cli children — orphaned acp-server.js processes accumulate
description: Observed 2026-07-03: 17 orphaned acp-server.js node servers (1-4 days old, reparented to systemd --user) left behind by dead kiro-cli/probe/test parents — kiro-cli does NOT kill its KAS child on exit, and stdio-transport servers with a dead pipe partner idle forever (~GBs of RAM). Upstream bug in kiro-cli, but cyril must defend: when cyril's bridge (or kas_*_smoke harnesses / probe scripts) spawns kiro-cli or acp-server.js directly, ensure the whole child process group dies with the parent (kill_on_drop + process-group kill on Linux; probes should terminate() in finally). Cleanup performed this session: killed all 17 (parent check: PPID == systemd --user).
acceptance_criteria: cyril exit (clean or panic) leaves no acp-server.js or kiro-cli descendants; probe/smoke harnesses kill children in teardown; a repeated spawn/kill cycle shows zero process accumulation.

notes.content: Closed: Fixed: PR #44 (108429a + 9ed33db portable fence probe). Repro: dropped_agent_process_kills_process_group (child + grandchild die on drop via process_group(0) + nix killpg guard; kill_on_drop backstop). Harnesses covered by inheritance; 62 probe scripts already had teardown.

title: W1 — /workflow command family driving _kiro/workflow/* ungated, with reattach-on-demand run lifetime
description:
The user-facing half of ROADMAP W1: cyril's own /workflow command family driving
_kiro/workflow/* directly, with runs modelled as persisted workspace objects that
are re-attached to on demand.

CONTROL PLANE (ADR-0011 -- ungated, client-owned)
Cyril never sets workflows.enabled. Live-verified 2026-08-08
(probe-kas-workflow-gateoff-2.16.0.py): listRecipes, list, listWatchHandlers, new
and invoke all answer with workflowsEnabled=false, and a gate-off invoke ran to
run_complete status=completed while delivering the full lifecycle stream. The
model therefore never gets run_workflow and cannot launch a run.

COMMANDS (v1 surface)
  /workflow recipes          -> listRecipes         (7 bundled)
  /workflow list             -> list                (REQUIRES explicit workspacePaths;
                                                     omitting them returns -32603
                                                     "workspacePaths is not iterable")
  /workflow run <recipe>     -> new + invoke
  /workflow attach <id>      -> follow an existing run
  /workflow status [<id>]    -> inspect
  /workflow cancel <id>      -> cancel
  /workflow resume <id>      -> resume

RUN LIFETIME -- reattach on demand
A run outlives both the session that started it and the cyril process that watched
it. v1 does NOT probe at startup; the user asks. The emitter buffers lifecycle
events before a client attaches and flushes them on subscribe, so a late attach
still receives the run's opening -- reattach does not lose the beginning.

RESPONSE PLUMBING -- the gap to close first
BridgeCommand::ExtMethod exists but DISCARDS the response (bridge.rs:1419-1430);
only errors surface, as BridgeError. Every command above needs its reply
(new -> {workflowId, initialState}; list -> {runs}; listRecipes -> 7 recipes).
ListKasHooks is the working template for a response-carrying bridge command,
including the workspace_paths argument this needs.

CAVEAT carried from ADR-0011: of the ten mutating verbs only `invoke` is verified
gate-off. A -32601/-32603 from cancel/pause/resume/retry/load/delete/update means
re-probe the gate, not a cyril bug.

Out of scope: rendering the run (panel/drill-in), model-launched runs, proxying
Kiro's four advertised commands (see cyril-oieu).
acceptance_criteria:
1. /workflow recipes, list, run, attach, status, cancel, resume work against a live KAS session with workflows.enabled NEVER set.
2. A response-carrying bridge command exists; replies reach the App as notifications rather than being discarded.
3. /workflow list sends explicit workspacePaths and never triggers -32603.
4. Attaching to a run started before cyril launched receives that run's opening events (flush-on-subscribe).
5. Kiro's four advertised workflow-* commands are never offered in autocomplete.
6. cargo test and cargo clippy -- -D warnings pass, including --features kas.

notes.content:
HAZARD 4 CHANGED IN 2.16.2 — new NodeState field `completionSignalSource`.
See cyril-6beh's 2026-08-08 note. Relevant here: src/workflow/run-disk-operations.ts
is a NEW module in the 2.16.1-2.16.2 range, and this issue's reattach-on-demand run
lifetime rests on run persistence semantics. Re-check list/load/attach against 2.16.2
before building against the 2.16.0 shapes.

title: KAS host-io: atomic write_text_file (temp + rename) to avoid corrupting files on partial write
description:
kas::host_io::write_text_file does tokio::fs::write (truncate + write) directly at the target path. A crash, disk-full, or error mid-write leaves a truncated/corrupt file in the user's working tree with the original content gone.

Since cyril is now the executor of the agent's writes (ADR-0003), durable writes belong at this layer: write to a temp file in the SAME directory, fsync, then atomic rename over the target -- matching the project's session-sidecar MOVED_TO cadence and the rust-best-practices atomic-write guidance. Decide behavior for symlink targets and permission/ownership preservation. Keep the existing mkdir -p (create_dir_all) for missing parents. Discovered during review of PR #34 (KAS-5a).
acceptance_criteria: An interrupted write never leaves a partial file at the target (original preserved, or fully-new content -- never half); temp + rename happens within the target's directory; empty-content and parent-dir-creation tests still pass; symlink-target behavior documented.

notes.content:
2026-07-01 issue-set review — PROMOTED P3->P2: since ADR-0003 makes cyril the executor of every KAS agent write, this is the only open issue whose failure mode is silent user-data loss (bare tokio::fs::write truncate-in-place, host_io.rs:52). Land before KAS becomes a daily driver.

Two footguns the plan must solve concretely (not just 'decide behavior'):
(1) Permission clobbering — NamedTempFile creates mode 0600 and persist() silently downgrades an existing 0644/0755 target. fs::metadata(target) + set_permissions on the temp BEFORE rename; umask-respecting mode for fresh files.
(2) Symlink write-through — rename replaces a symlink with a regular file (today's tokio::fs::write writes THROUGH it). canonicalize before choosing temp dir + rename target.

Implementation shape: whole sequence in ONE tokio::task::spawn_blocking with sync tempfile::NamedTempFile::new_in(parent) + write_all + sync_all + persist — single threadpool hop, temp auto-cleans on failure via Drop. Update the host_io.rs:9-18 doc comment (spawn_blocking is the sanctioned sync form). Dir-fsync optional: its failure mode is 'old content survives', which the AC permits; if added, unix-gate it (dir sync_all fails on Windows). Housekeeping: tempfile is currently dev-only in cyril-core (Cargo.toml) — promote via { workspace = true }.

Closed: Shipped: PR #49 merged to main (36b9272). All 6 ACs fenced: atomicity (write_atomic_unwritable_parent_errs_target_intact + SIGKILL oracle), temp-in-target-dir (message fence + TMPDIR oracle S18), empty/parents tests unedited, symlink behavior documented+fenced (write-through preserved, dangling refused), permission clobbering solved (mode preserved incl. 0600 anti-widening; fresh files umask-parity via File::create control oracle), tempfile promoted as kas-optional dep (zero default-graph edges). Live kas_fs_host_io_smoke passed against kiro-cli 2.11.0. Behavior changes (user-approved D1-D3): read-only targets refused, dangling symlinks error, unwritable-parent has no in-place fallback. Fixed in-branch: 7 pre-PR review findings (F1-F7, .cyril-0v42/review-decisions.md). Filed: none.

title: KAS-1: decide cyril's ACP clientInfo.name — it silently selects KAS persona, remote-tool allowlist branch, and hooks injection
description:
Discovered in the 2.13.0 wire audit (docs/kiro-2.13.0-wire-audit.md, memory reference_kiro_2_13_0_diff). KAS derives its entire client identity from the ACP initialize clientInfo.name via resolveAgentContext(env, clientInfo.name, caps). Only 'kiro-web' | 'kiro-ide' | 'kiro-cli' are recognized; ANY other name logs 'Unrecognized clientInfo.name: <x>, falling back to inferred client type' and becomes 'kiro-ide' (local). cyril currently sends its own product name, so on KAS it silently lands in the kiro-ide branch. Three downstream effects, all decided by this one string:

1. Remote-tool allowlist branch (resolveRemoteToolAllowlist): kiro-ide is CHANNEL-gated (stable -> [web_search], insider -> [web_search, searchMemories]); the memoryEnabled gate (searchMemories opt-in) exists ONLY on the kiro-cli branch. So cyril cannot reach the memoryEnabled path unless it presents clientInfo.name='kiro-cli'. (KIRO_LOAD_ALL_REMOTE_TOOLS=true forces '*' as a debug bypass.)
2. System-prompt PERSONA (getIdentity): 'You are Kiro CLI, an agent...' vs 'You are Kiro, an agentic...' (IDE). cyril inherits whichever persona its name maps to.
3. Hooks block is injected into the system prompt ONLY for kiro-ide (client === 'kiro-ide' ? hooksBlock : '').

DECISION NEEDED: what should cyril present as clientInfo.name to KAS? Presenting 'kiro-cli' gets the CLI persona + the memoryEnabled allowlist branch but misrepresents the client (also feeds AWS telemetry per reference_kiro_acp_telemetry, and cyril's real name is the honest value). Presenting cyril's own name is honest but forces the kiro-ide fallback (IDE persona + hooks block + channel-gated tools). This is a KAS-1 handshake knob distinct from cyril-nhzw (_meta.kiro.settings / AgentSettings flags) and cyril-evwh (engine selection + getAccessToken). Not blocking current v2 path. Relates: cyril-nhzw, cyril-evwh, cyril-6iek.


--- TRIAGE 2026-07-18 (hooksBlock verified from the extracted 2.13.0 KAS bundle, acp-server.js) ---

WHAT THE HOOKS BLOCK IS: a <hooks> system-prompt section briefing the MODEL on the
hooks feature: hook files at .kiro/hooks/<id>.json; "use the createHook tool, do NOT
write hook files manually with fs_write"; the full trigger vocabulary (UserPromptSubmit,
Stop, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PreTaskExec, PostTaskExec, PostFileSave, PostFileCreate,
PostFileDelete, SessionStart); action types (agent = append prompt to context, command =
shell with JSON on stdin); exit-code semantics (0 = success, stdout forwarded for
SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit/PreToolUse; 2 = BLOCK the action, stderr forwarded;
other = silent failure); the hook-file JSON schema; and IDE-only UI pointers
("explorer view 'Agent Hooks'", command palette "Open Kiro Hook UI").

KEY MECHANIC: this gate controls what the model is TOLD, not whether hooks RUN.
Execution rides the _meta.kiro.hooks handshake + host responders (KAS-7, cyril-jiyn).
Briefing keyed on clientInfo.name, machinery keyed on the _meta handshake -> the two
can desync into states Kiro never tested:
- name=cyril (kiro-ide fallback, today's accidental state): model briefed, but with IDE
  affordances that do not exist in a TUI -> wrong instructions to cyril users.
- name=kiro-cli: zero briefing while machinery can be live -> hook-injected context
  unattributed by the model; exit-2 PreToolUse blocks unexplained; "set up a hook"
  requests answered by hand-writing JSON (the exact failure the createHook prose exists
  to prevent).

BIGGER THAN THE AUDIT'S 3 BULLETS: the entire KAS base prompt is client-keyed —
getIdentity / getSessionTypes / getAutonomyModes / getChatContext / getSteering all
take client; hooksBlock is merely the only all-or-nothing section (ternary to "").

RECOMMENDATION: keep clientInfo.name = cyril's own name (honest; clientInfo feeds AWS
telemetry per reference_kiro_acp_telemetry; consistent with the be-legitimate stance
from the pi-kiro analysis). Treat the losses explicitly:
1. IDE persona: cosmetic.
2. memoryEnabled/searchMemories path unreachable: (a) upstream ask — recognize
   third-party ACP clients or key these gates off capabilities/_meta instead of the
   name; (b) before building any presentAs='kiro-cli' escape hatch, probe whether
   KIRO_LOAD_ALL_REMOTE_TOOLS=true already covers the power-user case.
3. Hooks-briefing mismatch: mitigable client-side — cyril injects a corrected hooks
   briefing (steering/context) when hooks are configured; couple with KAS-7.

DECIDE TOGETHER WITH cyril-jiyn (KAS-7); do not settle the name and the hooks
handshake independently.

--- DECISION RATIFIED 2026-07-18 (pause) / implemented on PR #61, pending merge ---
Honest default clientInfo {name:"cyril", title:"Cyril"} + opt-in [agent] present_as = "kiro-cli" knob (KAS-only, inert-with-warn on v2, title never impersonated). Recorded in docs/adr/0006-clientinfo-identity.md; fail-loud startup advisory because the classification is not exposed by the initialize response. The DECISION NEEDED block above is resolved; kept for history.

notes.content: Closed: Shipped: PR #61 merged to main (41c5a63). Decision (ADR-0006): honest default clientInfo {name:cyril, title:Cyril} + opt-in [agent] present_as=kiro-cli knob (KAS-only, inert-with-warn on v2, title never impersonated) + info startup advisory (classification not exposed by the initialize response). Fences: client_info_default_is_cyril_identity, client_info_present_as_kiro_cli, advisory_matrix (CI kas lane), present_as_inert_on_v2, invalid_present_as_falls_back_to_default_config; manual release-audit fence in conductor-spike README (probe-b, ALL-PASS live on 2.13.0). Probe C INCONCLUSIVE (TokenExpired) -> residue in cyril-jrl1 (with the memoryEnable {enabled:true} shape correction). Filed: cyril-ctnv (upstream ask), cyril-jmjb (spawn_bridge clump). 14-finding deep-review decision log at .cyril-0wyn/review-decisions.md.

title: KAS context breakdown: per-file items[] drill-in (deferred from KAS-2b aggregate bar)
description: KAS context_usage frames carry items[] on the contextFiles + sessionFiles buckets (probe-verified 2.10.0, .cyril-5et2/context_usage_raw.json); tools/yourPrompts/kiroResponses are aggregate-only (no items). KAS-2b (cyril-5et2) renders only the aggregate category bar and deliberately does NOT model or render the per-file items[]. A follow-up can surface a per-file drill-in for contextFiles/sessionFiles under KAS, reusing the v2 /context append_context_items render helper. Out of scope for the KAS-2b bar; this is the tracker for the deferred drill-in.

notes.content:
2026-07-01 issue-set review — SoC CORRECTION, reword scope: do NOT reuse app.rs append_context_items (app.rs:1017-1052). It lives in the App binary and parses raw serde_json::Value from the v2 commands/execute response; reusing it for KAS either re-serializes typed data back to JSON or leaks raw KAS JSON past convert into App — both boundary regressions (CLAUDE.md: App must not parse JSON), and it couples a KAS feature to the v2 response-format dialect. Note ContextBucket deliberately omits an items field with a comment naming this issue — the no-drill-in invariant is type-enforced (types/session.rs:264-269).
Right shape: typed ContextItem (name/tokens/percent/flags) on ContextBucket in cyril-core, parsed in convert/kas.rs, rendered in cyril-ui. Reuse the presentation FORMAT, not the function. Bonus: creates the destination for eventually migrating the v2 /context formatting out of app.rs — shrinking a pre-existing App-layer violation instead of doubling down on it.

2026-07-02 — Live per-file data confirmed from the KAS trace (kas-live-session-trace-2.11.0.jsonl, context_usage). contextFiles.items[] carried 47 entries, each {name, uri, tokens, matched, percent, progressivelyLoaded}. The typed ContextItem should include progressivelyLoaded (bool) — progressively-loaded skills show tokens:0 + progressivelyLoaded:true (ties to _kiro/progressive_context). So the fields to model: name, uri, tokens, percent, matched, progressivelyLoaded. Data is fully present on the wire; this is purely convert+render work. Breakdown buckets seen: contextFiles (has items[]), sessionFiles, kiroResponses, tools, yourPrompts (only contextFiles carries per-file items in this capture).

title: Model the full _kiro.dev/metadata surface; open up EffortLevel for backend-defined levels
description:
Effort levels are NOT a closed wire set — they are schema-negotiated per model. The backend's ListAvailableModels returns additionalModelRequestFieldsSchema per model; Anthropic models advertise effort under output_config (low/medium/high/xhigh/max), the newly added GPT models (e.g. gpt-5.6-terra, in the catalog as of 2026-07-14) under reasoning with a DIFFERENT enum. This invalidates the 'closed set on the wire' doc comment on EffortLevel (crates/cyril-core/src/types/session.rs:23): a GPT-style level reaching EffortLevel::from_wire drops to None with a debug log and the toolbar badge silently vanishes.

Two parts:
1. Open up EffortLevel: keep the known variants for typed use, add a fallback that preserves and displays the raw wire string (e.g. Other(String)) instead of dropping unknown levels. Update the doc comment — the set is per-model, backend-defined.
2. Model everything on _kiro.dev/metadata so additions are visible. Currently parsed in convert/kiro.rs: contextUsagePercentage, credits/turnDurationMs (metering), inputTokens/outputTokens/cachedTokens, effort. Anything else present on the wire should either be parsed into the notification or logged at debug when an unrecognized top-level key appears — the point is to KNOW a new field landed (backend rollouts add fields with zero binary change; the metering fields and the 2.12.1 refusal object both arrived this way). The refusal object itself stays with cyril-h8zb (related).

--- Authoritative field inventory (2026-07-14, carved 2.12.1 tui.js handleMetadataUpdate + live captures) ---

v2 _kiro.dev/metadata carries exactly, per the frontend consumer:
1. sessionId — routing guard (Kiro TUI drops frames whose sessionId != current session). Cyril routing gap filed separately.
2. contextUsagePercentage — parsed.
3. meteringUsage[] {value, unit, unitPlural} — cyril sums value; unit/unitPlural dropped (aggregate is fine, but note the per-entry shape).
4. turnDurationMs — parsed.
5. effort — parsed, BUT presence-sensitive on the wire: tui.js checks `"effort" in e` and an explicit `effort: null` is a badge-CLEAR signal. Cyril's convert warns 'present but not a string' and ignores it, and UiState effort is sticky — so an engine-initiated clear is dropped. Mitigated partly by cyril clearing effort on model change; still model the tri-state (absent=no-change / null=clear / string=set).
6. refusal {category, explanation, recommendedModel} — dropped; stays with cyril-h8zb (related).
7. stopReason (e.g. 'CONTENT_FILTERED') — dropped on this path; cyril-h8zb.

NOT on v2 metadata (do not add here): the token/status/usedTools cluster (totalTokens, uncachedInputTokens|inputTokens, outputTokens, cacheReadInputTokens|cachedTokens, cacheWriteInputTokens, status, usedTools, promptTurnSummaries, elapsedTime) is KAS-only — it rides session_info_update kind='turn_completion', which convert/kas.rs currently drops by design; that belongs to KAS-2b scope. Cyril's existing inputTokens/outputTokens/cachedTokens parse on the v2 metadata path has never been observed in committed captures (those names are the LEGACY fallbacks in the KAS normalizer) — keep it, but treat as unconfirmed-on-wire.
acceptance_criteria: Unknown effort level strings render in the toolbar instead of disappearing; EffortLevel doc no longer claims a closed wire set; every currently-known _kiro.dev/metadata field is either parsed or explicitly ignored with a comment; an unrecognized top-level metadata key produces a debug log naming the key; existing metadata tests still pass plus new coverage for the open-enum path and unknown-key logging.

notes.content: Closed: Implemented on feat/cyril-1gim (commit 3766c17): EffortLevel opened with Other(String) fallback, tri-state EffortUpdate (absent/null/string) modeled end to end, turnDurationMs parsed independently and merged order-independently via TurnMetering::merge_pending (credits now Option<f64> — no fabricated figures), full kiro.dev/metadata field inventory with unknown-key debug logging. 1095 tests green, clippy clean.
Migrated legacy external reference: gpt-models-effort-schema-2026-07

title: Resolve dead public diff-highlighting API and stale docs
description: Review finding #17: public diff-tint highlight helpers have no production callers while docs claim they are active and audits carry exemptions. Decide compatibility/deprecation, then wire or remove the API and stale documentation.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Public API compatibility is explicitly decided.
- [ ] Documentation matches production behavior.
- [ ] Unused audit exemptions and fabricated no-color fallback paths are removed.

title: acp rpc layer buffers notifications unboundedly under UI stall (no agent-side backpressure)
description: Tracking note from the 2026-07-01 issue-set reliability review — filed so the failure signature is searchable; no action until observed. The vendored agent-client-protocol read loop pushes every notification through incoming_tx.unbounded_send (rpc.rs handle_io) and spawns each handler as its own local task, which then awaits cyril's BOUNDED inbound channel (cap 256, bridge.rs:16/374). Verified during review: no deadlock is possible at the rpc layer (responses resolve inline; the 32-slot command channel circular wait is not realistically reachable) — but no backpressure ever reaches the agent process either. If the App stalls (worst realistic case: tty flow-control-stopped via Ctrl+S while terminal.draw blocks, app.rs:228+) during a heavy KAS streaming turn, the unbounded queue plus parked handler tasks grow without bound for the duration of the turn. Memory growth bounded by turn size, not a deadlock. Related: cyril-9akh lives in the same rpc.rs notification-vs-response plumbing.

title: KAS-5b follow-up: honor terminal/create outputByteLimit (truncate at char boundary)
description: KAS-5b (cyril-ufie) ships terminal/output with truncated:false and the full combined output. acp CreateTerminalRequest carries output_byte_limit: Option<u64> (ACP: when output exceeds the limit, the Client truncates from the BEGINNING to stay within it, at a UTF-8 char boundary, setting truncated:true). title: Enter-while-busy silently drops the user's message (regression from cyril-84ca off-loop guard)
description:
Regression introduced by cyril-84ca (PR #22): pressing Enter (non-slash text) while session.status()==Busy silently drops the user's message.

ROOT CAUSE: app.rs submit_input() (crates/cyril/src/app.rs:640) has NO busy guard. On Enter it take_input()s (clears the box), add_user_message()s (commits the text to the visible chat), set_status(Busy)+set_activity(Sending), then sends BridgeCommand::SendPrompt. After cyril-84ca the bridge's one-turn guard rejects a second SendPrompt mid-turn with BridgeError{operation:'prompt', message:'a turn is already in progress'} (bridge.rs SendPrompt guard). So the message is committed to chat and the input cleared, but it is NEVER sent to the agent — only an error system message appears.

BEHAVIOR CHANGE: pre-cyril-84ca the blocked command loop QUEUED the second SendPrompt and ran it as a sequential second turn after the first completed (message eventually sent). Post-cyril-84ca it is rejected (message lost). Live on main in the window between cyril-84ca merging and cyril-bm1j (K1b) landing — cyril-84ca blocks cyril-bm1j, so this PR merges first.

SECOND AFFECTED PATH: dispatch_code_command's Prompt branch (app.rs:1043) programmatically emits SendPrompt with no busy check; a /code-triggered prompt arriving mid-turn is rejected the same way, and its already-committed user text is never sent.

UI INCOHERENCE: UiState's BridgeError handler (crates/cyril-ui/src/state.rs:638) only add_system_message()s — it does NOT clear activity. So set_activity(Sending) from the rejected submit regresses the spinner from Streaming/ToolRunning back to 'Sending', the user sees 'prompt failed: a turn is already in progress', and then turn 1 keeps streaming — a sequence that did not occur pre-cyril-84ca.

PROPER FIX: this IS 'the latent second-prompt-mid-turn bug' that cyril-bm1j (K1b) is designed to fix by routing Enter-while-busy to SteerSession when status==Busy and input is non-slash. If the pre-K1b window matters, a minimal interim guard in submit_input (don't commit/clear + show a 'turn in progress' hint, or drop the second send before mutating UI) closes it without the full K1b UX.

Found by /code-review of PR #22.
acceptance_criteria: Submitting non-slash text while session.status()==Busy must not silently drop the message: either route it to SteerSession (K1b) or, at minimum, leave the input uncleared/uncommitted and surface a clear 'turn in progress' affordance, with no orphaned activity state (no spinner regression to Sending, no BridgeError-only dead end). The /code Prompt path (app.rs:1043) must likewise not lose its injected prompt mid-turn. Regression test: with a Busy session, submit Enter and assert the message is not lost and activity/status stay consistent.

title: Parse _meta.kiro.toolName / mcpServerName in convert/kiro.rs — trusted tool identity instead of LLM-authored titles
description: v2 tool_call / tool_call_update notifications carry a canonical, NON-model-authored tool identity in _meta.kiro: toolName (the real tool name) and mcpServerName (set ONLY for MCP-served tools, so a non-empty value is the trusted discriminator for a genuine MCP tool call vs a shell command whose output the model authored). The visible title is LLM prose — for the todo_list tool it reads like "Creating task list: ..." — so title can never identify a tool reliably. Kiro Crew keys its dashboard and security gating on this channel; cyril convert layer currently never reads _meta.kiro and docs/kiro-acp-protocol.md does not document it. Bonus unlocked by this channel: v2 never emits the ACP plan update (confirmed through 2.14.0) — the agent task list is the todo_list tool call, identified only via _meta.kiro.toolName, with the FULL list (never a delta) in rawOutput. Also note the related echo quirk: kiro camelCases snake_case rawInput keys on echo, so any key matching must read both spellings.
acceptance_criteria: convert/kiro.rs parses _meta.kiro.toolName and _meta.kiro.mcpServerName from tool_call and tool_call_update into ToolCall as Option<String> fields (Option for absent values, no sentinels; Kiro deviations stay in convert/kiro.rs, never mod.rs); merge_update preserves both fields when an update omits them; any tool-identification logic (e.g. todo_list detection) keys on toolName, never title; tests cover a fixture with _meta.kiro populated and one without (fields None); docs/kiro-acp-protocol.md documents the _meta.kiro identity channel and the rawInput camelCase echo quirk.

notes.content: Source: github.com/kirodotdev/kirocrew @ e44259ce, src/kiro_crew/acp/_dispatch.py (_kiro_tool_name, _kiro_mcp_server_name) + acp/types.py (KIRO_TOOL_TODO_LIST). Engine-side symbol cited by Crew: kiro_tool_identity_meta. Diffed against docs/kiro-acp-protocol.md 2026-08-04; see memory reference_kirocrew_platform.

Deep-dive addendum (docs/kirocrew-deep-dive.md): session/request_permission is identity-POOR — no kind, no _meta, truncated title. KiroCrew caches rawInput + trusted identity per toolCallId at the ToolCall notification and joins at permission time; the approval overlay must show the recovered real command (never the LLM-authored title), and gate fail-closed when _meta identity is absent. Permission response must echo the agent-provided optionIds exactly (allow_once/allow_always on kiro; differs per vendor; legacy options may omit kind). Cache needs a size cap (KiroCrew: 256, cleared per prompt).

title: KAS shell pipelines survive terminal cancellation
description: While implementing cyril-6bol, the selected-shell lifecycle fence proved that terminal/release killed only the outer shell process. Once a pipeline child had started, it survived release long enough to perform a delayed side effect; CancelRequest inherited the same process-only kill path. The terminal owner must isolate each Unix command in a process group and terminate the tree on kill/release/cancel/drop; native Windows explicit lifecycle paths must use taskkill /T /F with direct-child kill as a fallback.
acceptance_criteria: release_kills_child_and_frees_id starts an operator pipeline, waits until its child is live, releases it, and proves no delayed marker appears. cancel_reaps_sessions_running_terminals does the same through BridgeCommand::CancelRequest. Existing kill/output/status and dropped-owner lifecycle fences remain green.

notes.content: Closed: Fixed in PR #80 (ce0ea4f): process-tree fences — process_group(0)+killpg on unix, taskkill /T /F helper on windows — on kill/release/cancel

title: KAS-8 — Surface _kiro/safety/* Infrastructure Safety gate (can block tool calls)
description:
KAS-8 functional gap. `_kiro/safety/{statusChanged,propertiesChanged}` — Infrastructure Safety gate, added in kiro-cli 2.8.0 (embedded @kiro/agent). Cedar/AWS-governance signals that CAN BLOCK A TOOL CALL.

Why this matters more than the other notification gaps: it is ENFORCEMENT, not display. cyril's KAS-2a unknown-variant debug! arm silently drops these today, which means cyril can present a tool as runnable that KAS will refuse, or miss a posture change mid-session. Every other dropped notification just loses information; this one desyncs cyril from what KAS will actually permit.

SCOPE:
- Add a converter arm for `_kiro/safety/statusChanged` + `_kiro/safety/propertiesChanged` (pairs with the KAS-2c GovernanceSource sub-trait — same Cedar/governance family).
- Reflect a safety-blocked tool call in the UI (don't render it as a plain pending/allowed tool).
- Surface the safety status/posture so the user understands why a tool was refused.

REFS: covenant capabilities/safety/*.d.ts (on-disk @kiro/agent 0.3.257; NOT yet in the curated docs/kiro-kas-acp-covenant.md catalog — added after 0.3.224); ROADMAP KAS-8 coverage matrix; memory reference_kiro_2_8_0_diff (notes the safety gate). Probe the live shapes before implementing (no probe exists yet).

notes.content:
LIVE PROBE 2026-07-31 (2.16.0, probe-kas-safety-fork-load-2.16.0.py). The surface
is REACHABLE but INERT on this account.

Gate found and satisfied: capabilitiesFrom() reads
`infrastructureSafety: kiroMeta.infrastructureSafety === true`, i.e.
initialize.clientCapabilities._meta.kiro.infrastructureSafety. Advertising it
(plus c2sViews) is what earlier probes never did.

Result with the capability advertised:
  _kiro/safety/getProperties -> {"properties": []}   (real response, NOT -32601)
  _kiro/safety/statusChanged / propertiesChanged pushes: ZERO across
  initialize + session/new + a full turn.

Reading: the method is wired and answers, but there are no Cedar/AWS-governance
properties configured for this account, so nothing to report and nothing to
enforce. The BLOCKING behaviour this issue cares about cannot be observed
without an org policy attached — that is an account/backend precondition, not a
client one.

Actionable now: model `{properties: []}` as the empty-but-valid response shape,
and keep the unknown-variant arm from silently dropping statusChanged /
propertiesChanged. Do NOT infer from zero pushes that the notifications are
dormant in the product — we only established they are dormant HERE.

Capture: experiments/conductor-spike/kas-safety-fork-load-2.16.0.jsonl
Migrated legacy external reference: ROADMAP:KAS-8

RE-RUN WITH BOTH HALVES SATISFIED — 2026-08-01, still inert
(probe-kas-inconclusive-rerun-2.16.0.py, capture kas-inconclusive-2.16.0.jsonl).

The prior probe was under-specified: the gate is
  _infraSafetyEnabled = clientSupportsSafety && (monitorEnabled || enforceEnabled)
and that run advertised the flags but NOT the capability. This run satisfied both:
  clientCapabilities._meta.kiro.infrastructureSafety = true
  initialize._meta.kiro.settings.infraSafetyMonitor = {enabled:true}
  initialize._meta.kiro.settings.infraSafetyEnforce = {enabled:true}
(settings at INITIALIZE, so they bridge over the backend flags — the same lever that
DID unlock subagentOrchestration in the same session, which proves the mechanism works
and this is not another wiring mistake.)

Result: _kiro/safety/getProperties -> {"properties": []}, and ZERO
statusChanged/propertiesChanged frames across initialize + session/new + two turns,
one of which ran a shell command (the classic thing an enforcement gate would block).

CONCLUSION, now properly grounded rather than under-specified: the safety surface is
wired and answers, but this ACCOUNT has no Cedar/AWS-governance properties attached, so
there is nothing to report and nothing to enforce. Observing the BLOCKING behaviour
requires an org policy — an account/backend precondition cyril cannot create.

Actionable regardless: model {properties: []} as the empty-but-valid shape and keep the
unknown-variant arm from silently dropping statusChanged/propertiesChanged, so the day a
policy IS attached cyril degrades visibly rather than silently.

title: CYRIL_WSL_DISTRO non-Unicode value silently treated as unset (.ok() collapses missing vs corrupt)
description: process_wsl_distro (crates/cyril-core/src/platform/path.rs, the OnceLock init) reads the distro with std::env::var("CYRIL_WSL_DISTRO").ok(), collapsing VarError::NotPresent and VarError::NotUnicode: a corrupt (non-Unicode) distro value silently degrades to no-distro passthrough with no log, contradicting CLAUDE.md Silent Failure Prevention (distinguish missing from corrupt; audit .ok()). Surfaced by PR #89's post-PR review (finding 2), which fixed the identical collapse on CYRIL_AGENT_LOCATION in bind_agent_location; this is the pre-existing cyril-8tq6 twin, deferred to keep that PR's scope tight.
design: Mirror bind_agent_location: match on VarError, warn on NotUnicode(raw) with the raw value, fall back to None. The adjacent current_dir().ok() is fine — an unavailable cwd is not config corruption. Optional fence: a unix child test alongside env_non_unicode_falls_back_via_child_process in tests/win_wsl_wiring.rs (run_child already takes OsStr values).

title: Amend .cyril-6bol/spec.md: four decisions shipped without being written back
description: The cyril-6bol deep review found the implementation deliberately deviates from spec.md in four places where the decision was made and reviewed but the artifact never amended: (1) PowerShell compound commands collapse exit codes to 0/1 (findings.md #4 ratified the tradeoff; the spec edge row still says "Preserve the exit code"); (2) simple POSIX/fish commands run via an injected `exec ` prefix for signal fidelity — top-level shell builtins (cd/export/ulimit/source) now fail 127 and builtin-named commands bind to external binaries, which restores pre-PR direct-argv parity but contradicts B8 "no grammar translation" as written; (3) the PATH scan is capped at 256 entries (MAX_PATH_ENTRIES) while spec line 16 promises an unqualified PATH fallback; (4) the "Out of scope" rows for cancellation/reaping and output-drain overlap work the spec itself forces (cyril-2z9g tree fences, cyril-r3t6 create-time drain) and should acknowledge it. Text-only change to .cyril-6bol/spec.md on the PR branch or post-merge.

title: KAS-5b follow-up: reap/kill a session's live terminals on cancel/turn-end (orphan-on-cancel)
description: KAS-5b (cyril-ufie) spawns child processes on the bridge for terminal/create and reaps them on terminal/{release,kill} (the normal KAS flow: create->wait_for_exit->output->release). But if a turn is CANCELLED mid-command, KAS may not send release -> the child keeps running until it exits naturally (e.g. a 60s sleep = a 60s orphan on the bridge process). Scope: on session/cancel (and/or turn-end) kill that session's still-running terminals, keyed by session_id in the terminal registry. Needs the registry to track session_id per terminal (it carries sessionId on every request). Decide policy: kill-on-cancel vs let-finish. Out of KAS-5b's first cut (the happy-path lifecycle); this is the leak-on-cancel edge.

notes.content:
2026-07-01 issue-set review:
(1) TRIGGER SITE unnamed in the issue — mechanism (TerminalRegistry, owned by KiroClient at client.rs:26) and trigger (run_loop's Cancel arm bridge.rs:582-598 + TurnCompleted observation) sit on opposite sides of exactly the seam cyril-g9vt deferred. Decide JOINTLY with cyril-g9vt whether this is the ADR-0004 seam's first consumer. Minimal, proportionate option for a P3 leak fix: share Rc<TerminalRegistry> between KiroClient and the loop (same LocalSet thread; registry stays sole owner of process lifecycle) and call reap_session(session_id) from the Cancel arm. A third ad-hoc wiring (e.g. App sending a new reap BridgeCommand) would erode both this and g9vt.
(2) 'Keyed by session_id' should mean a session_id FIELD on Entry (from CreateTerminalRequest.session_id) + linear-scan reap_session — terminal id stays the primary key; a secondary index is over-engineering for a handful of terminals. Reap must follow the existing take-then-await pattern (no RefCell borrow across .await, terminal_io.rs:238-249).
(3) Policy recommendation: apply the existing KILL semantics (id stays valid, partial output cached), NOT release — KAS may still send terminal/output/release for those ids after the cancel, and kill-semantics lets them resolve instead of erroring -32602. Cancel-only for the first cut; reap-at-turn-end can race an in-flight release.
(4) INTERACTION with cyril-r3t6 (see its note): a cancelled turn whose command already wrote >64KB is wedged on the full OS pipe and never exits naturally — kill-on-cancel must also cover pre-wait children, and .kill_on_drop(true) at create is a cheap backstop.

Closed: Fixed: PR #48 (5f97307). Cancelled sessions' running terminals are reaped from run_loop's CancelRequest arm via shared Rc<TerminalRegistry> (session_id on Entry, linear-scan reap_session, KILL semantics — ids stay valid, in-flight children killed through their owning wait). Cancel-only per the issue's first-cut policy. Repro fences: cancel_reaps_sessions_running_terminals (end-to-end, alive-asserted pre-cancel), reap_session_kills_only_that_sessions_children_and_keeps_ids, reap_session_kills_child_owned_by_pending_wait.

title: Steering receipt: parse+strip the [STEERING <id>: note] trailer the model emits, reconcile onto the steer echo
description:
Evidence: AWS GenerateAssistantResponse prompt logs (2026-07-23, private workspace — NOT committed) show `_session/steer` reaches the model as its own user turn:

    [LIVE STEERING - New message from user]
    <user_message id="steer-<uuid>">TEXT</user_message>
    IMPORTANT: ... Use this exact format:
    [STEERING steer-<uuid>: <describe what you did or why it was not applicable>]

The model DOES comply — the captured assistantResponse ends with a well-formed
`[STEERING steer-<uuid>: ...]` trailer (pos 1588 of 1927, i.e. a tail trailer).

cyril has zero handling: the marker rides the AgentMessage stream and renders as raw prose
in the transcript. Meanwhile the SteerEcho chip sits at `applied` with no explanation.

The receipt id shares the id space with the wire queue id: the committed KAS capture
session_info_update_steering_queued.json carries a messageId of the same `steer-<uuid>`
shape. So id-based correlation to the SteerEcho is viable.

Work:
1. Pure parser in cyril-core/types/steer_receipt.rs — harvest complete markers out of a
   streaming buffer; compute the withheld tail so a partially-streamed marker never flashes.
2. UiState: harvest on AgentMessage append, reconcile onto the matching SteerEcho
   (id match, else the single unambiguous id-less Queued echo), keep the note.
3. chat.rs: render the note under the applied steer echo.

Conservative bias: never strip more than a well-formed marker. A `[STEERING ...` that never
terminates commits as ordinary text (todays behaviour, no regression).

Full structural findings: docs/kiro-prompt-assembly.md.

title: Watch: KAS 0.8.0 new surface _kiro/knowledge/indexing{Started,Completed} + _kiro/sandbox/applyConfig
description: The only net-new _kiro/* methods in @kiro/agent 0.3.299->0.8.0 (73->76, zero removals). Pairs with expanded local-embedding code (Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 feature-extraction pipeline; 'semantic search (MiniLM) or keyword search (BM25)') => local knowledge-base semantic index with progress notifications, plus dynamic sandbox reconfig. No cyril task consumes these today; log as future surface if a knowledge/RAG progress UI or sandbox-control feature is scoped. Re-check each release whether they start arriving unsolicited (would need tolerant ext-notification handling).
acceptance_criteria: Tracked; revisit at next kiro-cli release audit

notes.content:
LIVE-PROBED 2026-07-02 (probe-kas-knowledge-indexing-2.11.0.py). indexing{Started,Completed} = agent->client extNotifications (fire-and-forget; no client cap needed). Started {sessionId,name,fileCount}; Completed {sessionId,name,status,itemCount?} (itemCount only status='success'). TRIGGER: bind custom agent w/ resources.knowledgeBases[] via set_config_option {configId:'mode', value:'<agentId>'} (custom file agents appear as mode values) -> syncActiveAgentKnowledge at session setup/mode switch. KB schema {type:'knowledgeBase', source:'file://<rel>', name?, description?, indexType?:fast|best, include?, exclude?, autoUpdate?}. KEY: fast=BM25 local completes instantly; best=Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 via @huggingface/transformers allowRemoteModels=true + empty cache -> first use DOWNLOADS from HF hub -> Started fires WITHOUT Completed (>25s). Verified in code: (1) KasEngine drops unknown _kiro/* frames to Ok(None) — test kas_engine_drops_unknown_ext_frame (KAS-2a, cyril-j16p); (2) session_info_to_notification (kas.rs) handles only turn_end + context_usage, all other kinds -> _ => None. So both indexing notifications AND steering_queued/cleared drop gracefully; no crash/hang, no client capability handshake change. The knowledge TOOL (agent 'knowledge search') arrives as an ordinary ACP tool_call and already renders. => This issue is PURELY OPTIONAL display work: to show indexing progress, add two receive-side arms in convert_ext_notification for _kiro/knowledge/indexing{Started,Completed} + new internal Notification variants + a UI element (progress must tolerate 3 states: success+itemCount / failed / never-Completed while a ~90MB HF download runs). cyril SENDS nothing for this. _kiro/sandbox/applyConfig = elective client->agent send (mid-session sandbox toggle), likely out of scope. steer/clear tracked separately in cyril-vgcm (K1/KAS-steering track).

--- DESIGN SKETCH (2026-07-02, PROPOSAL — not built). A knowledge progress panel styled like crew_panel (bordered block, cyan ` knowledge ` title, `{icon} ` + bold-white `{name:<20}` + status, `+N more` overflow). One row per base; spinner (SPINNER_CHARS) while between Started/Completed, ✓ green (success)/✗ red (failed) once settled. Each row = one wire event:
  ⠹ downloading -> indexingStarted (best/first-use, ~90MB HF download, no Completed yet)
  ⠋ indexing    -> indexingStarted {fileCount}   (fast/BM25)
  ✓ indexed·Nit -> indexingCompleted status=success itemCount=N

  │⠹ api-docs             downloading model… ~90MB                               │

title: KAS-8 — Model _meta.kiro.hookConfirm + KAS agent-file hook types; render Stop-hook confirm dialogs
description:
From the 2026-07-17 KAS agent-file schema export (kiro-cli 2.13.0 / @kiro/agent 0.18.2; docs/kiro-kas-agent-*-schema-2.13.0.*, experiments/kas-agent-schema-export/): KAS agent files can embed inline hooks (landed 2.12.3) with a 'confirm' block that is honored on the Stop/agentStop trigger — when the agent tries to end its turn, the user is asked confirm.question with confirm.options[]; run:true options execute the hook command (whose output decides {continue, reason}), run:false options skip it and, with continueReason set, convert the turn-stop into keep-working with that reason fed to the agent (verified in src/hooks/triggers/stop.ts).

Wire shape (rides plain ACP, no new method): synthetic pending tool_call (toolCallId hook-confirm-<uuid>, kind 'other') tagged _meta.kiro.hookConfirm {kind:'stop', hookName, question} -> standard session/request_permission (optionId=option.id, name=label, kind=allow_once if run else reject_once) -> terminal tool_call_update with _meta.kiro.hookConfirm.decision.

Cyril work: (1) model the _meta.kiro.hookConfirm payload in convert/kas.rs (pending + decision variants) per the model-full-wire-surface rule; (2) render hook-confirm approvals as a distinct dialog (hook name + question) instead of a generic tool permission — note cyril filters kind-Other tool_calls from display, so without the _meta tag the pending marker is invisible and the permission prompt shows with no context; (3) verify the permission-response path returns arbitrary optionIds — a confirm block can have MULTIPLE reject_once options distinguished only by optionId/continueReason (cyril-qo13 fixed first-option-only for kind-keyed responses; confirm that fix covers this shape); (4) optionally: type the agent-file HookDocument/HookConfirm/HookAction shapes (committed JSON Schemas are the reference) for any future hooks-panel display of KAS inline hooks — current hooks panel models v2 HookInfo {trigger, command, matcher} only.

Semantics caveats for tests: confirm is Stop-trigger-only (schema allows it anywhere; other triggers ignore it); with no UI attached KAS skips confirm-hooks entirely, so absence of the dialog is not absence of the hook.
acceptance_criteria: convert/kas.rs parses _meta.kiro.hookConfirm (pending question + terminal decision) with unknown-field logging; approval overlay shows hook name + question for hookConfirm requests; regression test proving a 3-option confirm (run/skip/keep-working) can return each optionId; decision recorded on KAS inline-hook display in the hooks panel.

notes.content: WIRE-VERIFIED 2026-07-17 (probe-kas-hook-confirm-2.13.0.py, capture kas-hook-confirm-2.13.0.json, all 6 verdicts PASS): (1) pending tool_call hook-confirm-<uuid> kind=other + _meta.kiro.hookConfirm {kind:stop, hookName, question}; (2) requestPermission options run:true->allow_once, run:false->reject_once; (3) continueReason injected as NEW human message wrapped <HOOK_INSTRUCTION>...</HOOK_INSTRUCTION> + graph restart — agent obeyed it (HELLOTURTLES); (4) terminal tool_call_update carries decision=<optionId> with status=FAILED for reject_once picks — rendering caveat: a successful keep-working choice arrives as a failed tool call; (5) once-per-turn guard onAgentStopHooksExecuted (shared-graph-nodes.ts): stop hooks fire at most ONCE per turn, continuation runs unguarded to end_turn; (6) handshake gate = clientCapabilities._meta.kiro.hooks {enabled:true, v2:true} — v2 activates the standalone .kiro/hooks/*.json loader; fresh-git-dir ACP session counted workspaceTrusted.

title: KAS-2b — Live context-usage breakdown bar (session_info_update:context_usage)
description:
On KAS (v3), the per-category context breakdown is PUSHED proactively on the wire — so cyril can render a live categorized context bar (Files / Tools / Prompts / Responses) in the toolbar WITHOUT the user running /context. On v1/v2 the breakdown only exists as the pulled /context command response; the streaming _kiro.dev/metadata notification there carries only the scalar contextUsagePercentage.

WIRE SHAPE (probe-verified, kiro-cli 2.8.0, 2026-06-19, live KAS turn):
- session/update -> session_info_update, _meta.kiro.kind == 'context_usage', payload {usagePercentage, breakdown?} (covenant ContextUsageBreakdown).
- breakdown = 5 buckets {contextFiles, tools, kiroResponses, yourPrompts, sessionFiles}, each {tokens, percent, items?}.
- ~6 frames pushed per turn.

CONSTRAINTS THAT SHAPE THE UI (all probe-verified):
1. tools bucket is AGGREGATE-ONLY — items is structurally absent (live: {tokens:33703, percent:3.4}). Only contextFiles/sessionFiles ever carry items[]. Do NOT build per-tool drill-down; the wire cannot support it on either engine.
2. breakdown is OPTIONAL PER FRAME — some context_usage frames carry usagePercentage only (breakdown absent). Retain last non-absent; treat absence as 'no update', not 'cleared' (same discipline as the effort field).
3. cyril's existing /context path (kiro.dev/commands/execute) is REJECTED by KAS (-32603 'no persistence classification'). Must read the streaming notification, not the command surface.

MAPPING: breakdown is richer than cyril's flat ContextUsage/TokenCounts — either map usagePercentage to ContextUsage + extend, or model the breakdown as a new type. The itemized buckets can reuse the existing render helper append_context_items (crates/cyril/src/app.rs:900), today wired only to the pulled /context path.

DEPENDS ON: KAS-2a (walking skeleton — turn renders+ends via session_info_update:turn_end; not yet filed). Part of the KAS-2 _kiro/* dialect track, anchored on KAS-0 (cyril-atjw).

REFS: probe experiments/conductor-spike/probe-kas-context-breakdown-2.8.0.py; ROADMAP KAS-2b (docs/ROADMAP.md:179).
acceptance_criteria:
* On the KAS engine, cyril renders a live categorized context bar fed by session_info_update:context_usage frames — no /context command issued.
* Per-frame 'breakdown absent' is handled: last breakdown retained, not cleared.
* tools bucket renders as an aggregate row (no per-tool UI); contextFiles/sessionFiles render itemized when items[] is present.
* v1/v2 engine behavior is unchanged (still uses the pulled /context command response).
* State + render tests cover (a) a breakdown-absent frame and (b) the aggregate-only tools bucket.

notes.content:
2026-06-21 — Re-confirmed the 5-bucket breakdown independently (experiments/conductor-spike/probe-kas-context-shows-steering.py): contextFiles itemized the file the agent read; tools aggregate-only (33703 tokens, no items); the v2 /context (kiro.dev/commands/execute) rejected. RELEVANT NEGATIVE for this bar: the breakdown has NO steering bucket and does not itemize steering docs. Steering is a SEPARATE channel (_kiro/steering/documents_changed catalog + session_info_update:steering_inclusion) — so do NOT try to source an 'active rules/steering' view from the context bar; it isn't there. See memory reference_kiro_kas_filematch_steering_source.

Closed: Implemented and merged via PR #33 (merge 9aca2fe); follow-up review fixes in 56f57ec. Deferred items tracked: cyril-1116 (per-file drill-in), cyril-mdbp (narrow-terminal overflow), cyril-cx27 (SessionController lifecycle divergence).
