title: KAS host callbacks gated by cargo feature, not bound engine — implement ADR-0001 capability accessors or amend the ADR
description:
Found by the 2026-07-01 KAS implementation review (SoC lens). In a --features kas build running the V2 engine, KiroClient still answers kiro/auth/getAccessToken with the real token and answers fs/* and terminal/* callbacks if the subprocess sends them (client.rs:192-281) — despite V2Engine advertising no such capabilities, and despite ADR-0001's design intent that these are surfaces 'KAS implements and v2 does not.' The cargo feature quietly replaced the bound engine as the availability gate for host callbacks.

ADR-0001's consequences also promise the capability sub-trait mechanism ('the accessor pattern is introduced in KAS-1, where AuthResponder gets a real implementation and consumer') — no AuthResponder trait exists anywhere; auth landed as a static feature-gated handler, fs/terminal as feature-gated KiroClient overrides. The ADR text is stale.

Practical risk is LOW today (the subprocess is kiro-cli; v2 never sends these callbacks — the code says so at client.rs:23-24,180). But the next capability (KAS-7 hooks, _kiro/safety/*, cyril-3ald) will copy whatever precedent exists, so resolve before then. DISTINCT from cyril-g9vt: that issue is about the ADR-0004 stage-interception seam; this one is engine-vs-feature gating of responder availability.

Cheapest fix short of sub-traits: have the responders consult the bound engine (KiroClient already holds Rc<dyn Engine>) before answering — refuse with method-not-found when the engine does not advertise the capability. Either way, amend ADR-0001's consequences to match what shipped.

--- UPDATE 2026-08-01: ADR-0001 amended; the escape hatch in the old acceptance criteria is CLOSED ---

ADR-0001 now carries a host-callback capability-adapter amendment (driven by the 2026-07-30 architecture review, Candidate 01). It does NOT take the "document feature-level gating as the accepted design" branch — it takes the opposite one, so that branch of the old acceptance criteria is void. What the ADR now decides:

1. THE ADAPTER SET IS DATA, ADVERTISEMENT IS DERIVED FROM IT. `Engine::adapters() -> Adapters { auth, host_io, hooks }` (each optional), with client_capabilities() derived from that set rather than written independently. The `as_*`-accessor phrasing from the original ADR is WITHDRAWN: a defaulted downcast-style accessor leaves advertisement and execution as two facts a future engine can desynchronize — exactly this bug. Deriving one from the other makes the invariant mechanical instead of conventional. The review reached the same conclusion independently via its deletion test ("deepen around the Engine module").

2. REFUSE, DO NOT DEFAULT. An engine with no adapter for a family refuses those callbacks. It must NOT fall through to the protocol-default null: unhandled_ext_response's own doc comment records that the agent reads a null result as SUCCESS WITH AN EMPTY RESULT — the silent-failure shape this codebase forbids.

3. THE INVARIANT IS PER DIRECTION — new since this issue was filed, and it is a counterexample to the naive form. ADR-0010 (2026-08-01, cyril-gk17) established that _kiro/hooks/list is BIDIRECTIONAL: under kas_hooks="host" cyril serves it inbound; under "kas" cyril SENDS it outbound as a BridgeCommand and the agent executes hooks itself. So "kas" mode legitimately advertises hooks ({enabled:true, v2:true} in engine.rs) with NO inbound adapter, while client.rs:57 installs an empty HookRegistry. "An absent execution adapter cannot be advertised" is therefore FALSE as stated — it holds only for the INBOUND direction. Do not reconcile this by treating the empty registry as the adapter: an empty adapter standing for "absent" is a sentinel, against the project's no-sentinel rule. Hooks is the one family where cyril is both server and client of the same method name; the Hooks adapter must hold both directions or it will fit host mode and silently exclude the shipped kas mode.

Now on the critical path: cyril-g9vt's mediator dispatches to this adapter set, so this lands first.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A --features kas build running the v2 engine REFUSES getAccessToken / fs/* / terminal/* (method-not-found or equivalent — never the protocol-default null), test-fenced.
2. Engine exposes the adapter set as data and derives inbound client_capabilities() from it; no engine can advertise an inbound capability it installs no adapter for.
3. One test walks the adapter set to prove advertisement and execution reachability TOGETHER (separate tests of those two facts are explicitly insufficient).
4. The per-direction carve-out is fenced: kas_hooks="kas" advertises hooks with no inbound adapter and is NOT reconciled by an empty-registry sentinel.
5. Stale AuthResponder consequence text in ADR-0001 corrected. (DONE 2026-08-01 — struck and marked superseded.)

notes.content: Closed: Shipped: PR #82 merged to main (05ffd29). All ACs fenced: AC1 refusal fences (auth/typed-fs/kiro-fs-walked/terminal), AC2 Adapters-as-data + derived client_capabilities free fn, AC3 adapter_matrix_advertise_iff_answer (mutation-checked, per-bit fs pairing), AC4 registry Option-iff-Inbound + Outbound-refuses-inbound fences, AC5 pre-done, AC6 live v2 full pass + live KAS session/fs/hooks pass with run_command failure parity-proven pre-existing. Fixed in-branch: cyril-y14u. Filed: cyril-y14u, cyril-cb93.

title: Docs claim Windows spawns wsl kiro-cli acp — code spawns kiro-cli acp natively
description:
The WSL spawn was never wired as a default: --agent-command defaults to ["kiro-cli","acp"] on every platform (crates/cyril/src/main.rs:27) and AgentProcess::spawn execs it verbatim with no platform-conditional wrapping (crates/cyril-core/src/protocol/transport.rs:174). On a Windows machine with the Kiro MSI installed, PATH resolves kiro-cli to the native kiro-cli.exe — no WSL involved.

Three places still describe WSL spawning as current behavior:
1. CLAUDE.md 'Platform Constraints': 'Windows: spawns wsl kiro-cli acp; requires WSL with kiro-cli installed and authenticated'.
2. transport.rs:181-182 comment: 'Windows spawns wsl kiro-cli acp and has no Unix process groups'.
3. README Prerequisites WSL-only line (docs/ROADMAP.md already flags dropping it now that Kiro ships a native Windows binary).

This misdirection has real cost: it produced wrong platform-reach conclusions twice, most recently the 2.16.0 wire-audit voice addendum ('Kiro voice unreachable on cyril's entire platform matrix'), corrected 2026-08-01 (see the addendum in docs/kiro-2.16.0-wire-audit.md and memory feedback_cyril_native_windows_not_wsl_ceiling).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] CLAUDE.md Platform Constraints describes actual behavior: native spawn by default on all platforms; WSL only via explicit --agent-command wsl kiro-cli acp; notes the path-translation caveat (companion issue)
- [ ] transport.rs:181-182 comment corrected (kill_on_drop backstop rationale restated without the WSL claim)
- [ ] README Prerequisites drops the WSL-only line (closes the ROADMAP line-41 item)

title: KAS settings sweep: 5/21 flags change the handshake; workflows adds 4 slash commands we never saw
description:
Systematic per-flag A/B of all 21 KAS client-settings keys
(probe-kas-settings-sweep-2.16.0.py, captures kas-settings-2.16.0-*.jsonl, FREE —
handshake + session/new only, no prompt turn).

THE MASTER LEVER, from the initialize handler: settings sent at INITIALIZE
override the BACKEND model-config feature flags, not just session config —

    const rawKeys = new Set(Object.keys(kiroMeta.settings));
    const bridgedIsFeatureEnabled = (feature) =>
      rawKeys.has(feature) ? isSettingEnabled(initSettings, feature)
                           : prev.isFeatureEnabled(feature);
    setModelConfigProvider(bridgeFeatureFlags(prev, bridgedIsFeatureEnabled));

So `initialize._meta.kiro.settings` is a client-side override of backend flags.
Prior probes only sent settings at session/new.

5 of 21 flags produce a handshake-visible delta:

  workflows          -> workflowsEnabled:true AND FOUR NEW SLASH COMMANDS:
                        workflow-run, workflow-status, workflow-cancel,
                        workflow-resume.  ** We never saw these. ** Every workflow
                        probe drove _kiro/workflow/* directly and never noticed the
                        command surface appear. This is the USER-FACING half of the
                        workflow feature and it is one settings key away.
  fta                -> adds MODE `functional_task_alignment` (7 modes -> 8)
                        and ftaEnabled:true
  goal               -> adds the `goal` command
  specPlan           -> specPlanEnabled:true
  steeringSupervisor -> steeringSupervisorEnabled:true — a field that does NOT
                        EXIST in session/new._meta by default (null -> true), so
                        it is invisible unless you ask for it

No handshake delta (13): checkpoint, codeIntelligence, compaction,
disableAutoCompaction, inlineAgents, knowledge, largeToolOutputHandler,
semanticReview, sessionEviction, tangentMode, thinking, todoList, toolSearch.
These may still change IN-TURN behaviour (prompt content, tool selection); this
sweep only observes the handshake.

TWO INCONCLUSIVE, NOT NEGATIVE — my own probe was under-specified:
  subagentOrchestration — no handshake delta even via the initialize bridge. But
    the surface it drives is chosen during PROMPT construction
    (getDelegationToolId(getModelConfigProvider().isFeatureEnabled(...)) in
    prompts.ts), which a handshake-only sweep cannot see. Needs ONE paid turn with
    the flag set at initialize to settle whether OrchestrateSubAgent appears.
    Do not read this as confirming cyril-ucii's "backend-gated" conclusion.
  infraSafetyEnforce / infraSafetyMonitor — no delta, but the gate is
    `clientSupportsSafety && (monitorEnabled || enforceEnabled)` and THIS SWEEP DID
    NOT ADVERTISE `infrastructureSafety`. The arms were missing half the condition.
    Re-run with the capability advertised before concluding anything for cyril-3ald.

notes.content:
The  arm of this sweep concluded the user-facing half is 'one settings
key away'. True but no longer load-bearing for cyril: the four slash commands and
five tools that key unlocks are exactly what cyril has decided NOT to enable
(ADR-0011), because the methods route ungated and enabling the tools lets the model
launch runs. The other four handshake-visible flags (fta, goal, specPlan,
steeringSupervisor) are unaffected by that decision and remain the useful part of
this sweep.

Correction to the note above: its first line lost a word to a shell substitution.
It should read "The `workflows` arm of this sweep concluded ...". No other line was affected.

title: Render KAS agent-subtask pipelines from the existing tool-call stream (ToolKind::Other filter exception)
description:
Render KAS OrchestrateSubAgent / agent-subtask pipelines from the tool-call stream cyril ALREADY receives — no new protocol required.

Trace-verified (experiments/conductor-spike/kas-live-session-trace-2.11.0.jsonl, KAS 0.8.0): subagent runs surface as ordinary session/update tool_call + tool_call_update frames tagged _meta.kiro {kind: "agent-subtask", agentSubtaskId: <uuid>}, with the plan in the initial tool_call's rawInput (invoke path {name, prompt, explanation, contextFiles, preset}); group by agentSubtaskId. Sample: 5 subtask groups, 44 tool_call + 113 tool_call_update + 8 session_info_update.

THE BLOCKER IS CLIENT-SIDE: these arrive with ACP kind "other", which cyril filters as agent "planning" steps (CLAUDE.md ToolKind::Other rule), so the entire run is dropped. cyril must check _meta.kiro.kind == "agent-subtask" BEFORE that filter. That exception is the prerequisite for any KAS crew rendering.

Split out of cyril-6beh (2026-07-26 PR #68 review): 6beh keeps the deferred _kiro/workflow/* protocol scope, which must not ship until an emitter exists. This issue is the near-term half and is actionable today.
design:
IMPLEMENTATION DESIGN — trace-verified emission shape (from experiments/conductor-spike/kas-live-session-trace-2.11.0.jsonl, KAS 2.11.0/0.8.0):

1. KAS subagent runs surface as ordinary session/update tool_call + tool_call_update frames, tagged _meta.kiro: {kind: 'agent-subtask', agentSubtaskId: <uuid>}. Sample: 5 distinct agentSubtaskId groups, 44 tool_call + 113 tool_call_update + 8 session_info_update carrying the tags (frames/subtask 9-93).
2. The PLAN is in the initial tool_call's rawInput. Invoke path (verified in trace): {name, prompt, explanation, contextFiles, preset}. Orchestrate path (from KAS buildSchema, NOT yet wire-verified): {task, stages[]{name,role,prompt_template,depends_on,inlineAgent?}, repeat{maxIterations,stopCondition,onMaxIterations}}.
3. Group frames by agentSubtaskId to reconstruct which stage is which + live progress; title = 'Sub-agent: <name>'.

*** KEY GAP / real blocker for the observe path ***: agent-subtask tool_calls arrive with ACP kind == 'other'. cyril FILTERS ToolKind::Other from display (CLAUDE.md: 'Tool calls with kind == ToolKind::Other are planning steps... filtered from display'), so cyril currently DROPS the entire subagent run. FIX: check _meta.kiro.kind == 'agent-subtask' BEFORE the ToolKind::Other filter (one branch). This is the unblock, not a missing emitter.

LIVE ORCHESTRATE CAPTURE (2.14.1): harness built + committed (experiments/conductor-spike/probe-kas-orchestrate-capture-2.14.1.py) but BLOCKED — all on-disk kiro tokens expired (kiro-auth-token.json exp 2026-07-19, kiro-auth-token-cli.json exp 2026-06-10; auth_kv not plaintext-extractable), so KAS rejected the getAccessToken reply with -32000 TokenInvalidError after 7 retries and the turn never orchestrated. The probe is correct (reached KAS, faithful kiro-cli-chat acp --agent-engine kas spawn); it needs a FRESH token (run right after kiro login, or wire OIDC refresh into the probe). So the orchestrate {task,stages,repeat} on-wire rawInput + loop_iteration behavior remain live-unverified; the KAS bundle schema+executor confirm they exist.

SPLIT EXECUTED (2026-07-26, PR #68 review): this issue IS the near-term half — render agent-subtask pipelines from the existing tool-call stream, gated only by the ToolKind::Other filter exception. The deferred _kiro/workflow/* live-progress protocol is cyril-6beh and must not be built against until an emitter ships.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Tool calls tagged _meta.kiro.kind == "agent-subtask" survive the ToolKind::Other filter and reach the UI.
2. Calls sharing an agentSubtaskId render as one grouped run, not N unrelated tool calls.
3. The initial tool_call's rawInput (name/prompt/explanation) is surfaced as the run's plan.
4. A regression fence asserts an agent-subtask tool_call with kind "other" is NOT filtered, and that a genuine planning step with no _meta.kiro.kind still IS.

notes.content:
2.16.0 LIVE RE-CONFIRMATION (paid capture, kas-turn-2.16.0.jsonl +
kas-orchestrate-stages-2.16.0.jsonl): the invoke-path shape this issue is built
on is unchanged from the 2.11.0 trace and is what cyril will actually see —
OrchestrateSubAgent is gated OFF by default (see cyril-ucii), so the invoke path
is the only subagent surface reachable today.

Confirmed on the wire at 2.16.0:
  tool_call        _meta.kiro {kind:"agent-subtask", agentSubtaskId:<uuid>}
                   rawInput {name, prompt, explanation, contextFiles}
                   title "Sub-agent: general-task-execution"
                   acp kind "other"   <-- the ToolKind::Other exception this issue needs
  tool_call_update same agentSubtaskId, status pending -> in_progress -> completed
                   (the in_progress update carries title: null)
  tool_call_update title "Subagent Response", rawInput {response, files}

Note the lifecycle: three updates share one agentSubtaskId, and the middle one
has a null title — so grouping must key on agentSubtaskId, never on title.

RENDER CONTRACT CAPTURED 2026-08-01 (kas-inconclusive-2.16.0.jsonl). With subagentOrchestration enabled at INITIALIZE, the OrchestrateSubAgent tool_call carries _meta.kiro.pipeline:
  {groupId: 'pipeline-<task-slug>', stages:[{name, role, status, dependsOn[], agentSubtaskId}]}
That is the grouping key this issue needs: agentSubtaskId links each pipeline stage to its individual agent-subtask tool_call/tool_call_update frames, and dependsOn gives the DAG edges for rendering. Envelope: title 'Orchestrate Sub-agent', acp kind 'other' (the ToolKind::Other exception), status in_progress.

Note this is the ORCHESTRATE path, which requires the client to opt in. With it off (cyril today) only the INVOKE path appears — rawInput {name,prompt,explanation,contextFiles}, title 'Sub-agent: <name>', no pipeline meta. Rendering must handle BOTH.

ITERATION TRAP (measured 2026-08-01, kas-repeat-shape-2.16.0.jsonl). Across an OrchestrateSubAgent repeat loop the _meta.kiro.pipeline stage entry is REUSED: groupId constant, stages[] keeps one entry per stage, status cycles pending->running->completed->running->completed. Rendering from pipeline status alone makes a completed stage appear to un-complete on the next iteration.

The discriminator is agentSubtaskId — 6 agent-subtask frames carried 2 DISTINCT ids, one per iteration. So: group the pipeline by groupId, but key each RUN of a stage on agentSubtaskId. Same class of bug as the workflow nodePath/iteration finding.

ERROR-PATH TRAP — measured 2026-08-01 (probe-kas-orchestrate-variants-2.16.0.py, capture kas-orch-variants-2.16.0.jsonl). This is the most dangerous rendering finding for this issue.

On an ABORTED OrchestrateSubAgent run (repeat exhausted with onMaxIterations:'abort'), the payload CONTRADICTS the status:

  tool_call_update status = 'failed'          <-- the ONLY truthful signal
  _meta.kiro.pipeline stages = [('pick','completed')]   <-- says completed
  rawOutput.response = 'Pipeline completed: 2 stages finished. ...'  <-- says COMPLETED

So every per-stage status reads 'completed' and the human-readable summary literally begins 'Pipeline completed' on a run that FAILED. A renderer keying off stage status, or echoing rawOutput.response, will show a green successful pipeline for an aborted one.

RULE: the top-level tool_call_update.status is the only authority for pipeline outcome. Treat _meta.kiro.pipeline[].status and rawOutput.response as per-stage/for-display detail that is NOT outcome-bearing.

Status transitions observed (abort): tool_call in_progress -> update in_progress(running) -> in_progress(completed) -> in_progress(running) -> in_progress(completed) -> **failed**. Note the Orchestrate tool_call stays in_progress for the whole loop and only flips at the end.

Contrast, satisfied stopCondition (early exit): 1 iteration, ends status 'completed', 'Pipeline completed: 1 stages finished.' Clean.

Also: rawOutput carries its OWN nested pipeline summary {groupId, stages[{name,role,status,dependsOn,agentSubtaskId}]}, in addition to _meta.kiro.pipeline on the frames.

title: Windows ProcessTree drop path kills the shell but leaks pipeline children
description: impl Drop for ProcessTree (terminal_io.rs) is cfg(unix)-only. On native Windows an un-reaped drop (LocalSet teardown, bridge death, app exit) falls back to tokio kill_on_drop(true), which terminates only the outer shell process — pipeline children survive, exactly the leak the cyril-2z9g tree fences exist to prevent. The explicit terminate_process_tree (taskkill /T /F) path covers kill/release/cancel but not drops. The type name promises cleanup one platform does not get on the drop path. Fix: a Windows drop-path tree kill (or a documented decision that drops may leak there and why), plus a Windows-gated fence once runnable-in-CI.

title: Dead stream_buffer module: StreamBuffer has zero production consumers
description:
Found while probing cyril-nd4h (see .cyril-nd4h/findings.md, finding #2).

crates/cyril-ui/src/stream_buffer.rs defines StreamBuffer (a debounced
streaming-text accumulator that flushes on natural boundaries or after a
timeout). It is exported as `pub mod stream_buffer` from cyril-ui/src/lib.rs
but has ZERO references anywhere outside its own file — grep -w for
'StreamBuffer' and 'stream_buffer' across crates/ returns only lib.rs:12 (the
mod declaration) and the file itself. It is never constructed in production.

cyril-nd4h removes the ui.stream_buffer_timeout_ms config field, which was the
only thing that referenced this component's existence (and it too had no
consumer). That closes the config-surface half; the dead module itself is out
of nd4h's scope and remains.

Decide: (a) delete the module, matching the cyril-85py precedent for
zero-reader code, or (b) wire it into the streaming path it was written for —
agent text currently accumulates in UiState.streaming_text with no debounce
(CLAUDE.md 'Streaming Content Model'), which is plausibly what StreamBuffer was
built to solve.

title: KAS-1 — Engine selection + _kiro/auth/getAccessToken responder (the entry gate)
description:
The precondition for every KAS milestone below. Without a host-supplied token, every KAS turn dies immediately ([TokenInvalidError] ... Host refresh callback returned no access token).

SCOPE (ROADMAP KAS-1, docs/ROADMAP.md:154):
- Make the KAS spawn real: the AgentEngine gate from KAS-0 (cyril-atjw) resolves the KAS engine to a live process; default stays v2. All new KAS code lands behind the 'kas' cargo feature from KAS-0.
  NOTE / CORRECTION: the engine flag was renamed 'kas' -> 'v3' as of kiro-cli 2.8.0 (probe-verified: 'kas' is rejected, possible values are v1/v2/v3; spawn is 'kiro-cli acp --agent-engine v3'). 2.7.1 accepted 'kas'. Resolve the engine string per installed version, don't hardcode 'kas'.
- Implement a '_kiro/auth/getAccessToken' server->client request responder: reply {accessToken, expiresAt, profileArn}. KAS validates expiresAt > now + ~3 min and REQUIRES profileArn (backend 400s 'profileArn is required' without it).
- Token sourcing — MIRROR Kiro's own responder, don't just read the sqlite row. Kiro (crates/chat-cli-v2/src/auth/{kas_token,refresh_coordinator,social,builder_id,external_idp}.rs): (1) resolves the active token across THREE types — social (GitHub -> kirocli:social:token, carries profile_arn), AWS Builder ID, external IdP (kirocli:external-idp:token); (2) proactively OIDC-refreshes before the ~3-min pre-expiry buffer via a lock-guarded refresh_coordinator; (3) answers {accessToken, expiresAt, profileArn}. A naive 'read kirocli:social:token and return it' responder breaks on the refresh buffer (the failure our probes hit) and on Builder-ID/external-IdP users. Cleanest: DELEGATE to kiro-cli's own auth rather than reimplement OIDC refresh + multi-type resolution.
- This makes cyril a CUSTODIAN of a kiro credential — handle as such (no logging, read-only, minimal lifetime). See ROADMAP Open Tension #7.

This is the AUTH half of the initialize._meta.kiro (KiroClientMeta) handshake; the SETTINGS half is cyril-nhzw (AgentSettings).

REFS: ROADMAP KAS-1 (docs/ROADMAP.md:154); covenant docs/kiro-kas-acp-covenant.md (KiroClientMeta handshake); memory reference_kiro_kas_launch_contract.
acceptance_criteria:
* Engine-select plumbing resolves the KAS engine to a live spawn (version-correct flag: v3 on >=2.8.0, kas on 2.7.1); default remains v2.
* '_kiro/auth/getAccessToken' responder replies {accessToken, expiresAt, profileArn} and is exercised in a gated end-to-end smoke against a live KAS session.
* Auth-responder unit test covers the reply shape AND expired-token rejection (expiresAt <= now + ~3 min).
* profileArn is always present in the reply (Builder-ID / external-IdP users included), sourced by delegating to kiro-cli's own auth.
* Credential is never logged; token read is read-only and minimal-lifetime.

notes.content:
2026-06-21 — FREE PATH CONFIRMED; de-risks the entry gate (auth responder is no longer a hard prerequisite for a first live KAS turn).

Verified live: kiro-cli 2.8.1, @kiro/agent 0.3.257, experiments/conductor-spike/probe-kas-direct-spawn-2.8.1.py. KAS's selectAuthProvider resolves a --auth=user|machine|acp-callback flag (default user). The two spawn shapes differ:
  - WRAPPER spawn `kiro-cli acp --agent-engine v3` injects --auth=acp-callback -> KAS calls _kiro/auth/getAccessToken back on cyril -> the responder (this issue's main scope) is MANDATORY. This is the [TokenInvalidError] failure our earlier probes hit.
  - DIRECT spawn `node --experimental-wasm-modules <.../@kiro/agent/dist/server/acp-server.js> --transport=stdio` with NO --auth flag -> default FileAuthProvider reads ~/.aws/sso/cache/kiro-auth-token.json and self-refreshes via the file's refreshToken. _kiro/auth/getAccessToken fired 0 times across a full initialize + session/new + tool-using turn (stopReason end_turn). stderr logged "[INFO] Auth: default token file".

IMPLICATION: a first live KAS turn (cyril-j16p / KAS-2a) is reachable with ZERO credential-custodian code as long as the user has run `kiro-cli login`. Open Tension #7 moves OFF the walking-skeleton critical path.

SUGGESTED SPLIT (for triage, not yet applied):
  - tier-1 = free-path direct spawn, no responder. Unblocks the demo.
  - tier-2 = the _kiro/auth/getAccessToken acp-callback responder for the blessed wrapper lifecycle (kiro-cli token-sync + lock-guarded refresh-coordinator) and Builder-ID / external-IdP users.

Direct-spawn trade-off: cyril must locate the server entry (KIRO_KAS_SERVER_PATH env, else walk node_modules/@kiro/agent/dist/server/acp-server.js), the node runtime (KIRO_AGENT_PATH), and pass --experimental-wasm-modules — all of which the wrapper handles for free.

ROADMAP KAS-1 updated with this. Full --auth/--transport/sandbox flag contract + 5-tier auth priority in memory reference_kiro_kas_launch_contract.

2026-06-21 (fileMatch-steering probe session) — FOURTH token type for the tier-2 acp-callback responder, NOT covered by the three above: an IAM Identity Center / OIDC-PKCE login stores under auth_kv key `kirocli:odic:token` = {access_token, expires_at, refresh_token, region, start_url, oauth_flow, scopes} and carries NO profile_arn. For that case the matching profileArn lives in a SEPARATE row: auth_kv->`state` table, key `api.codewhisperer.profile`. Proven pitfall: pairing an OIDC accessToken with a DIFFERENT identity's profileArn (e.g. a stale ~/.aws/sso/cache/kiro-auth-token*.json, different account/region) -> backend 'Access denied'; accessToken and profileArn MUST be the same identity. Reinforces 'don't naively read one sqlite row': the responder must resolve profileArn per token type (social/Builder-ID embed it; odic splits it into state/api.codewhisperer.profile). Working assembly verified end-to-end in experiments/conductor-spike/probe-kas-filematch-steering-v2.py (odic access_token + state profileArn -> live KAS turn succeeded). Caveat for the direct-spawn 'free path': it reads ~/.aws/sso/cache/kiro-auth-token.json, but those files can be STALE/expired (they were expired this session for an odic-active user), so the free path depends on that file being kept fresh. See memory reference_kiro_kas_filematch_steering_source.
Migrated legacy external reference: ROADMAP:KAS-1

title: Absent contextUsagePercentage on kiro.dev/metadata stamps main context to 0.0 (sentinel fallback)
description: Discovered during cyril-fh06 (PR #54): real 2.4.1 captures contain v2 _kiro.dev/metadata frames with NO contextUsagePercentage (e.g. {"sessionId":…, "turnDurationMs":2281, "effort":"high"} in experiments/conductor-spike/trace-2.4.1-multi-subagent.jsonl). convert/kiro.rs warns and falls back to 0.0, so a main-session frame of this shape stamps the toolbar context-usage to 0.0% — a plausible-looking wrong value, violating the workspace 'errors are not default values' rule. Fix shape: make the notification field Option<f64> (absent = no-change, same retain-last discipline as effort) or skip the context update when the key is absent; keep metering/duration/effort applying. Left byte-identical in cyril-fh06 on purpose.
acceptance_criteria: A metadata frame without contextUsagePercentage leaves context usage unchanged while still applying its metering/duration/effort; a frame with the field still updates; regression test replays the captured no-context frame shape.

notes.content: Closed: Fixed: PR #56 (52fa590). Repro: convert::tests::metadata_without_context_retains_last_context (replays captured 2.4.1 duration/effort-only frame through to_ext_notification -> SessionController; failed red at Some(0.0) pre-fix). Companion fences: metadata_without_context_still_applies_metering_and_effort + cyril-ui toolbar retention test. context_usage is now Option<ContextUsage>; absent = retain-last, present-but-non-numeric warns with value.

title: KAS host-io Windows: verify terminal/create with a translated wsl$ UNC cwd
description: After cyril-8tq6, terminal_io::create's cwd (to_native_checked, terminal_io.rs:105) can become \\wsl$\<distro>\... on a Windows host with a WSL-native workspace. std::process::Command::current_dir with a UNC path works at the CreateProcess level but some programs (notably cmd.exe) refuse a UNC cwd. Today the same scenario fails anyway (a POSIX /home cwd does not exist on the host), so this is no regression — but Windows-host behavior is unverified. Verify on a real Windows+WSL host and decide whether terminal cwd needs special handling (e.g. refusing with a clear error).

title: K1a — Queue-steering wire + state plumbing
description: Wire + state machinery for Kiro 2.7.0 queue steering. Converter arm for _kiro.dev/session/update (steering_queued/consumed/cleared -> notifications), bridge SteerSession/ClearSteering as awaited _session/steer[/clear] ExtRequests with a -32601 emit-once unsupported gate, and SessionController/UiState mirrors (steering_depth, steering_unsupported, steering_queued). No UX — that is K1b.

title: Route _kiro.dev/metadata by params.sessionId — subagent metadata frames currently stamp the main toolbar
description:
v2 _kiro.dev/metadata frames carry a params-level sessionId, and during agent_crew runs subagent sessions emit their OWN metadata frames: the committed captures prove it (experiments/conductor-spike/trace-2.4.1-multi-subagent.jsonl has metadata frames for 5 distinct sessionIds; trace-2.4.1-tui-recorder.jsonl has 4). Kiro's own TUI filters them — carved 2.12.1 tui.js handleMetadataUpdate begins: let n=e.sessionId; if(n && n!==this.sessionId) return.

Cyril does not: client.rs ext_notification routes everything except ToolCallChunk as RoutedNotification::global, so MetadataUpdated from a subagent session is applied to the main SessionController/UiState. Consequences during any multi-subagent v2 turn: main toolbar context-usage % flickers with subagent percentages, subagent per-turn credits/duration are attributed to the main session, and a subagent effort value could overwrite the main badge.

Fix shape: extract params.sessionId in convert (or promote it in client.rs the way ToolCallChunk already does) and route MetadataUpdated scoped; frames with no sessionId stay global. Decide explicitly what a subagent-scoped metadata frame updates (likely: the subagent stream state or nothing, mirroring Kiro TUI's drop) — and keep main-session behavior byte-identical for single-session turns.
acceptance_criteria: MetadataUpdated from a frame whose sessionId matches a known subagent no longer mutates main-session context_usage/metering/effort; single-session metadata behavior unchanged (existing tests pass); regression test replays a main-metadata + subagent-metadata sequence and asserts main toolbar values come only from the main frame; frames without sessionId still apply to main.

notes.content: Closed: Fixed: PR #54 (8d28784). Repro: metadata_routing_tests::subagent_metadata_does_not_stamp_main_session (wire-shaped frames from trace-2.4.1-multi-subagent.jsonl replayed through real ext_notification + App routing contract). Companion fence: metadata_without_session_id_still_applies_to_main. Fix mirrors the ToolCallChunk scoped-promotion idiom; empty/absent sessionId stays global.

title: KAS-3 — Subagent rendering must handle dropped/empty/never-terminal results (upstream Kiro #9542)
description:
KAS subagent results can legitimately be empty, dropped, or never delivered — cyril's KAS-3 agent-subtask rendering (ROADMAP KAS-3; unfiled until now) must degrade gracefully. Surfaced by upstream Kiro bug #9542 (subagent "No result").

THREE upstream failure modes cyril will observe on the wire:
1. (v2) premature channel close: parent goes Idle before the subagent's `summary` is delivered -> stage result = "No result" (trace WARN: 'tool execution event for an agent not processing tools ... active_state: Idle, executing_subagents: {}').
2. (v3/KAS) null-response schema-validation fail: subagent hits max_tokens on long output -> response=null -> "No result". Intermittent, output-length-driven.
3. session-level channel corruption: a CANCELLED multi-stage `depends_on` pipeline leaves the multiplexer channel un-reset -> ALL subsequent subagent calls return "No result" until CLI restart.

cyril impact (cyril is an OBSERVER — can't fix upstream, must render robustly):
- Crew panel / SubagentUiState must NOT show a subagent as perpetually 'running' when its result is dropped/never-terminal. Treat a quiet subagent with no terminal result as a terminal 'no result / interrupted' state. On KAS the "No result" arrives as the parent's `orchestrate_subagent` tool_call_update content — render faithfully.
- HAZARD cyril can TRIGGER: Esc -> session/cancel during a KAS multi-stage subagent pipeline is exactly the Ctrl+C path that triggers upstream mode 3 (session-wide channel corruption). cyril should guard/warn, and if subagent results start coming back empty, surface a 'subagent channel may be wedged — /new to recover' hint.
- Repro/verify with the ACP wire recorder KIRO_ACP_RECORD_PATH=/tmp/acp-trace.jsonl ({ts,dir,msg} JSONL; lives in tui.js, confirmed 2.8.1).

Engine note: failure mode differs v2 vs v3. Related: cyril-9akh (notification-vs-response ordering race this validates), cyril-j16p (KAS-2a walking skeleton this builds on).

notes.content:
2026-07-01 issue-set review — split acceptance criteria BY ENGINE (current wording conflates v2 and KAS paths):
- The 'Crew panel / SubagentUiState must not show perpetually running' line applies ONLY to v2 failure mode #1. On KAS those components receive nothing (no list_update); feeding KAS subtask data into SubagentTracker would violate the CLAUDE.md separate-path rule.
- KAS modes #2/#3 belong to the greenfield KAS-3 subtask path: a distinct grouper keyed on _meta.kiro.kind == 'agent-subtask' / agentSubtaskId, with _meta parsing in convert/kas.rs producing engine-neutral typed fields (UiState never reads raw _meta). Nothing in the crates handles agent-subtask yet — KAS-3 is greenfield, right moment to pin this.
- The never-terminal inference (quiet subagent with no terminal result -> render interrupted) and the wedge heuristic (empty results -> hint /new) are stateful inferences that live in that KAS-3 component, NOT SubagentTracker.
- The orchestrate_subagent tool_call_update rendering approach and the App-altitude Esc-hazard guard are architecturally clean as filed.

title: All handled host callbacks cross the bridge mediator (ADR-0004 amendment)
description:
Deferred from KAS-5a (cyril-7bdu) during checkpointed-build. ADR-0004 decided that server->client host-io requests (fs, terminal) route THROUGH the bridge run_loop's host-io arm so the engine's capability sub-traits / a cyril-stages gate can observe/transform them. KAS-5a instead resolves fs DIRECTLY in #[cfg(feature=kas)] KiroClient overrides (kas::host_io::{read,write}_text_file) because: (1) the loop seam has no consumer yet — no stages gate exists (the codebase's engine.rs:12 rule says capability sub-traits land WITH their first consumer, not as consumer-less stubs); (2) routing through run_loop forces a #[cfg]'d run_loop parameter (can't cleanly cfg a single fn param) — either ship HostIoRequest+channel un-gated in every v2 build (violates ADR-0002 'default build links no KAS code') or maintain two cfg'd run_loop signatures; (3) the non-blocking invariant (KAS-5a claim C4) is already satisfied WITHOUT the loop arm — the acp ClientSideConnection spawns each inbound request as its own spawn_local task (rpc.rs:272, wired bridge.rs:390), so a direct async tokio::fs resolve is off-loop and never starves the loop.

WHEN TO BUILD THIS: when the first real consumer of the seam lands — a cyril-stages host-io gate (audit/policy/transform of file reads+writes+shell execs, ADR-0003/Phase 2) or KAS-7 hooks. At that point, move fs+terminal resolution behind a HostIoRequest channel + run_loop arm so the consumer can intercept, and resolve ADR-0002's cfg-threading (likely: gate the whole host-io module + a kas-only run_loop variant, or accept un-gated host-io once it's no longer kas-only). Until then, direct-resolve in the cfg'd overrides is the right altitude.

REFS: ADR-0004 (docs/adr/0004); .cyril-7bdu/falsifiable-design.md claim C3 + Negative-space #3; KAS-5a cyril-7bdu.

--- UPDATE 2026-08-01: deferral expired; scope widened; design settled in ADR-0004 amendment ---

Driven by the 2026-07-30 recent-hotspot architecture review (Candidate 01, its TOP recommendation) and now recorded as the ADR-0004 amendment. This is a DRIFT-CLOSURE ticket, not a new feature: ADR-0004's original Decision already routed "KAS-5 fs/terminal, KAS-1 auth later" through the loop. The three deferral reasons above, reassessed:

(1) "no consumer yet" — EXPIRED. The consumer is lifecycle unification, already visible as two ad-hoc escapes: the terminal-registry Rc grabbed out of KiroClient before the ACP connection takes ownership (cyril-3lh8, bridge.rs:586), and hook cancel handled inline in ext_notification (client.rs:199). Two adapters, two bespoke routes; a third capability invents a third.

(2) "forces a #[cfg]'d run_loop parameter" — DISSOLVED by our own later work. InternalChannels (bridge.rs:672) already threads a #[cfg(feature="kas")] field through ONE parameter, destructured with `..`. ADR-0002 is preserved by making the callback payload uninhabited in a default build (`enum HostCallback {}`): the select! arm compiles, its match is exhaustively empty, and no KAS code links.

(3) "non-blocking already satisfied without the loop arm" — CORRECT, AND CONCEDED. It is a constraint to preserve, not a benefit this delivers. Same for shutdown-abort: kill_on_drop(true) + LocalSet teardown already reap callback children; formalizing that is worth doing but is not a leak being fixed.

SCOPE IS WIDER THAN THE TITLE SUGGESTED. Not just host-io: every handled host-callback request AND control notification. Size from the variant count, not the family count — ~19 handled non-permission variants today: 7 typed acp::Client overrides, 5 ext requests, the 5 _kiro/fs/* ops added by ADR-0009 (which postdate the review), and 2 control notifications (hooks cancel/didChange).

DESIGN NOW SETTLED IN ADR-0004's AMENDMENT. Load-bearing points: the mediator is a TYPE with an accept()-style entry point (NOT more select! arms — run_loop is already ~1,405 lines), and it stays THIN. The review's deletion test concluded "deepen around the Engine module", so depth accretes on the ADR-0001 adapter set, not here; adding a capability must touch the mediator zero times. Cutover is sliced per adapter (Auth, then Host I/O, then Hooks), parity-preserving, deleting the direct paths it replaces.

SEQUENCING: blocked on cyril-b4y4 (review Candidate 02) and cyril-dn91. b4y4 amends ADR-0004's OWN turn-completion section — landing it first keeps ADR-0004 to one coherent amendment instead of two on overlapping ground, and lands this mediator in a run_loop that has already shed its inline turn policy. dn91 supplies the Engine-selected adapter set this mediator dispatches to.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Every handled host-callback request and control notification crosses one bridge-internal mediator type; the direct KiroClient paths it replaces are deleted.
2. The mediator has an accept()-style entry point that is unit-testable without the async bridge harness; run_loop's arm holds no callback policy inline.
3. A default (non-kas) build still links no KAS code — ADR-0002's compile-time posture verified, not assumed.
4. Seam scenarios prove: non-blocking mediation, ordered acceptance with concurrent resolution, bounded backpressure, callback-specific cancellation, responder drop, shutdown, and notification-before-error-response ordering.
5. Every handled callback variant has an exhaustive mediation-wiring case (~19 today).
6. Strict behavior parity per slice, confirmed against a live kiro-cli acp session for both engines.

title: Enable KAS v2 hooks: gate is _meta.kiro.hooks={enabled,v2}; agent executes hooks host-side
description:
The KAS v2 hooks subsystem is fully reachable, and cyril has never turned it on.
Live-verified 2026-07-31 (probe-kas-v2hooks-2.16.0.py, capture
kas-v2hooks-2.16.0.jsonl, kiro-cli 2.16.0 / KAS 0.27.8).

THE GATE (two earlier probes got this wrong):
  clientCapabilities._meta.kiro.hooks = { "enabled": true, "v2": true }
It must be an OBJECT. The bundle reads `kiroMeta?.hooks?.enabled` and then
`hooksConfig.v2 === true`; advertising the BOOLEAN `true` makes `?.enabled`
undefined and silently skips the whole block — which is what
probe-kas-pushed-methods-2.16.0.py did, and why _kiro/hooks/setEnabled answered
"not available when v2Hooks is disabled" in the RPC sweep.

HOOK FILES: <workspace>/.kiro/hooks/*.json, validated by kasHookFileSchema:
  { "version": "v1",
    "hooks": [ { name, description?, trigger, matcher?, action,
                 timeout?, enabled?, confirm? } ] }
  trigger (file, camelCase): preToolUse | postToolUse | sessionStart | stop
  action: discriminated union on `type` — command | prompt | agent

VERIFIED WORKING:
- _kiro/hooks/list  {sessionId, workspacePaths, includeDisabled} -> {hooks:[...]}
- _kiro/hooks/setEnabled {sessionId, hookId, enabled} -> {success:true}, both
  directions; it rewrites the enabled flag in the backing FILE.
- _kiro/hooks/didChange fires as a notification carrying the full registry.
- Hooks ACTUALLY EXECUTE. Both a sessionStart and a preToolUse hook ran during a
  normal turn; the host-side evidence file contained
  "cyril-audit-hook-fired-start | cyril-audit-hook-fired-pre".

WIRE SHAPE (differs from the file shape in two ways cyril must translate):
  { "id": "<absolute filePath>#hook-<n>",       // composite, not a bare name
    "name": "cyril-audit-pre",
    "action": { "type": "runCommand", "command": "..." },   // file says "command",
                                                            // wire says "runCommand"
    "_meta": { "trigger": "PreToolUse",          // PascalCase on the wire,
                                                 // camelCase in the file
               "source": "standalone-file",
               "filePath": "...",
               "enabled": true } }

ARCHITECTURAL FINDING — v1 and v2 hooks execute in DIFFERENT PROCESSES:
  v2 (this): the AGENT runs the command itself via its own processRunner.
             _kiro/hooks/executeHook is never sent to the client.
  v1:        the agent asks the CLIENT to run hooks (that is what the
             agent->client _kiro/hooks/{list,sessionStart,executeHook} are for).
So `_kiro/hooks/list` really is bidirectional, and WHICH direction is live depends
on which hook generation the client advertised.

SECURITY NOTE, worth a deliberate decision rather than a default: with v2 enabled,
a `.kiro/hooks/*.json` in the workspace causes the AGENT to execute arbitrary shell
commands on the host, and no session/request_permission was raised for either hook
in this capture. The workspaceTrusted flag feeds a `disabledReason:
"untrusted-workspace"` field, so trust state is the intended guard. cyril should
not advertise `hooks.v2` without deciding how it establishes workspace trust and
whether it surfaces hook execution in the transcript.

title: KAS allow_always consent-scope echo: live control probe, then optional consent passthrough on permission responses
description: Split from cyril-qo13 (its widened-scope halves b+c for KAS). The qo13 prove-it probe RESOLVED the allow_once case: the reference client itself omitted the _meta.kiro.consent echo on trace requests 8/9 (present on 6/7, all consentRound=1) and all four fs_writes completed -> consent echo is OPTIONAL for invocation-scope grants; cyril need not send it. UNVERIFIED remainder: allow_always. The reference outcome shape for allow_once was scope:'invocation'; presumably always-accept echoes scope:'session'|'always', and it is unknown whether KAS persists the grant scope WITHOUT that echo (schema-present != required, feedback_kiro_schema_vs_runtime). CONTROL PROBE: live KAS session (python raw JSON-RPC template in experiments/conductor-spike/), trigger fs_write approval, reply optionId:'always-accept' WITH NO consent _meta, then re-trigger the same capability+resource and check whether KAS re-asks (grant not persisted) or proceeds (persisted). If required: add an engine-conditional consent{capability,scope,workspaceRoot} passthrough on the permission response via convert/kas.rs (the KAS seam), echoing request _meta.kiro.consent.capability/workspaceRoot + scope derived from the picked option. Evidence base: experiments/conductor-spike/kas-live-session-trace-2.11.0.jsonl + .cyril-qo13/probe-findings.md.

notes.content:
CONSENT SHAPE DRIFTS ACROSS BUNDLES (2026-07-02, KAS modes probe — docs/kiro-kas-modes-2.10.0.md wire delta #4): the request-side consent _meta is not a stable struct. 2.10.0 bundle (@kiro/agent 0.3.299, modes-probe capture): {capability, resource, askType, triggeringResource, workspaceRoot} — consentRound ABSENT, triggeringResource present. 2.11.0 trace (0.8.0): consentRound present (=1 on reqs 6/7), no triggeringResource observed. Implication for the passthrough half of this issue: do NOT model consent as a typed struct with required fields — echo the request's consent object opaquely (serde_json::Value or all-optional fields), adding only the derived scope. A typed consent that requires consentRound or triggeringResource will break on the other bundle line. Raw evidence: experiments/conductor-spike/kas-modes-dumps/bug-fix.json (first permission frame) vs kas-live-session-trace-2.11.0.jsonl.

LIVE DATAPOINT (2026-07-02, qo13 C8 probe, KAS 2.11.0 direct-spawn): replied {outcome:{outcome:'selected',optionId:'always-accept'}} (NO consent _meta) to the first execute approval; turn proceeded BUT two further permission requests still arrived in the same turn (different resources/commands). Consistent with per-resource/per-capability consent scoping rather than the always grant failing outright — but ambiguous without inspecting the follow-up requests' consent.resource. The control probe this issue plans should compare same-resource re-asks specifically.

title: Render v2 model-refusal alerts: parse refusal object on kiro.dev/metadata (2.12.1)
description:
kiro-cli 2.12.1 adds Model Refusal Alerts: when the backend refuses (content policy / content filter), the v2 engine emits an optional refusal object on the kiro.dev/metadata notification — {category, explanation, recommendedModel} (camelCase on wire; confirmed from carved 2.12.1 tui.js handler: broadcastStreamEvent({type:'model_refusal', stopReason, category:r?.category, explanation:r?.explanation, recommendedModel:r?.recommendedModel})) — and metadata stopReason can be 'CONTENT_FILTERED'. The session/prompt response can also return ACP stop_reason: refusal.

Cyril today: to_stop_reason maps Refusal correctly and toolbar shows 'Refused' (red), but convert/kiro.rs kiro.dev/metadata parsing (to_ext_notification) reads only contextUsagePercentage/meteringUsage/tokens/effort — the refusal object is silently dropped. Kiro's own TUI shows a transient error alert plus a system chat message with the explanation (fallback text suggests switching model / new conversation / rewind). Cyril users get a bare 'Refused' with no why and no recommended model.

Scope: extend the MetadataUpdated notification (or add a dedicated notification) with Option<RefusalInfo {category, explanation, recommended_model}>, surface it in UiState as a system message + toolbar state. Guard partial updates per design principles (all three fields optional). Note: runtime emission not yet live-verified (cannot force a backend refusal on demand) — schema evidence is from binary serde strings + tui.js handler; per feedback_kiro_schema_vs_runtime treat wire keys as provisional until first live refusal capture. Stale doc comment types/session.rs:497-499 ('bridge currently hardcodes EndTurn') should be deleted in passing — bridge.rs:794 extracts the real stop reason.

2.12.3 audit addendum (docs/kiro-2.12.3-wire-audit.md): refusal handling grew in tui.js (8->13 tokens); 'refusal' is now a FIRST-CLASS stopReason zod literal with two emit paths -> model_refusal {stopReason, category, explanation, recommendedModel} (KAS/_kiro side). When implementing, tolerate stopReason 'refusal' in addition to metadata stopReason 'CONTENT_FILTERED'. Still no live refusal capture; keys remain provisional.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A kiro.dev/metadata payload carrying refusal {category, explanation, recommendedModel} produces a user-visible explanation in the chat (system message) and does not disturb existing metadata fields; 2) absent refusal field = no behavior change; 3) refusal with missing/partial subfields renders whatever is present without defaults or panics; 4) stale TurnSummary doc comment removed; 5) state + render tests per testing-layers convention.

Closed: Shipped: PR #79 merged to main (15b6c6f). All AC covered: refusal payload renders explanation as system chat message without disturbing sibling metadata fields (refusal_full + preserves_existing_fields + render fence); absent refusal = no behavior change (absent_unchanged); partial/corrupt subfields render what's present, no defaults/panics (partial_matrix + corrupt_* fences); stale TurnSummary doc comment deleted; state+render tests per testing-layers. Beyond AC per probes: Kiro's OR-condition (bare CONTENT_FILTERED alerts, fallback text), stopReason 'refusal' tolerance (2.12.3 addendum), per-turn dedupe, TurnSummary reconcile EndTurn->Refusal via shared StopReason::reconcile_refusal in BOTH state machines (toolbar reads UiState's summary). title: Two KAS probes write a live bearer token into their capture file
description:
FIXED 2026-07-31. Emit-time redaction retrofitted onto both named probes:

  probe-kas-compact-summarization-2.9.0.py
  probe-kas-orchestrate-wire-2.9.0.py

Both now define SECRET_KEYS + redact() and apply it inside rec(), so the real
token still reaches KAS and the frame shape survives, but the log gets
"<redacted>". Verified with a synthetic auth frame through each file's actual
extracted helper: bearer token, refreshToken (nested) and profileArn all
redacted; non-secret values and the key set preserved.

Scope widened slightly, deliberately:
- ALL FOUR bidirectional-logging probes now share ONE identical 13-key set
  (the two above, the canonical probe-kas-orchestrate-capture-2.14.1.py, and the
  new probe-kas-turn-traffic-ab-2.16.0.py). The canonical set gained
  profileArn/profile_arn/authorization/Authorization so there is one convention
  rather than three variants.

The "49 probes answer getAccessToken" concern in the original description is
narrower than it looks. The defect requires logging BOTH directions. Swept the 5
other probes that both answer getAccessToken and write a capture file
(custom-dag-live-2.16.0, hostinit-2.15.0, turnend-capture,
workflow-repeat-watch-2.16.0, workflow-runtime-2.16.0): all are structurally
immune — their rep()/send() writes only to the child process stdin, while the
file writer only takes RECEIVED frames. Confirmed empirically too (their
captures scanned clean before commit). So the real predicate is
"logs outbound frames", not "answers getAccessToken", and that set is now
fully covered.

Pre-existing captures on disk are out of scope here — see the account-id issue.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Neither probe writes an unredacted accessToken to its capture; verified by running the redact helper over a synthetic auth frame.
2. KAS still receives the real token (redaction applies only on the path to the log).
3. A grep over experiments/conductor-spike shows no probe persisting an auth reply without redaction.

notes.content: probe-kas-turn-traffic-ab-2.16.0.py (added 2026-07-31) would have been a THIRD offender — its client_to_agent records include our own reply to _kiro/auth/getAccessToken, which carries the live bearer token. Fixed at the source rather than post-hoc: the probe now scrubs at emit time via a SECRET_KEYS set (accessToken/access_token/profileArn/profile_arn/idToken/refreshToken/authorization), so its captures are committable by construction. Verified the scrub does not change the diff-acp-wire result. That emit-time scrub is the pattern to retrofit onto the two existing probes this issue tracks.

title: KAS terminal wait_for_exit stalls when a clean-exiting command leaves a daemonized pipe holder
description: A command that exits cleanly but leaves a background child holding the shared output pipe delays the terminal/wait_for_exit reply until that orphan closes the pipe: join_output (terminal_io.rs) joins the drain reader AFTER child.wait(), and the reader only reaches EOF when every writer fd closes. Measured in the cyril-6bol deep review with `sh -c "sleep 3 & printf done"`: child.wait() returned in 1.9ms, read_to_end in 3.00s — the wait reply is silently delayed for the whole window. kill/release recover via the process-tree kill; a CLEAN-exiting daemonizing command does not. The module doc claims the create-time drain prevents deadlocks and never mentions this bound. Fix direction: an exit-detection escape for the drain (e.g. bounded post-exit grace then snapshot what was read), plus a module-doc correction.

notes.content: Closed: Fixed: PR #83 (cde0ea9). Drain reader publishes into a shared buffer; join_output bounds the EOF join with a 500ms post-exit grace then snapshots (applies at wait/kill/release). Repro fence: wait_reply_not_held_hostage_by_daemonized_pipe_holder (3.08s stall red -> 0.64s green). Module doc corrected.

title: Surface meta.subcommands in help and autocomplete (10 of 24 agent commands advertise them)
description:
commands/available carries a meta.subcommands array that cyril's CommandInfo drops, so cyril's help and autocomplete never mention any subcommand. Users have to already know they exist.

NOT a wire bug — the mechanism works today. Verified at 2.14.2: args.value is a free-form string and the agent's own per-command parser splits subcommand + arguments. `_kiro.dev/commands/execute {command:{command:'context',args:{value:'show'}}}` returns the full context breakdown, so typing `/context show` in cyril already works via AgentCommand::execute's {value: args} path (commands/mod.rs:281-285). This is purely discoverability.

Advertised subcommands, captured live (2.14.2, v2, 24 commands total):
  /agent      selection  [create, edit, swap]
  /chat       selection  [save, load, new]
  /code       panel      [status, init, logs, overview, summary]
  /context    panel      [show, add, remove, clear]
  /effort     selection  [set-current-as-default]
  /goal       panel      [clear]
  /knowledge  panel      [show, add, remove, update, clear, cancel]
  /mcp        panel      [list, add, remove]
  /model      selection  [set-current-as-default]
  /tools      panel      [trust-all, trust, untrust, reset]

CommandInfo (crates/cyril-core/src/types/command.rs) models name/label/description/has_options/is_selection/is_local and discards the rest of meta (subcommands, hint, searchable). Adding subcommands is additive.

Worth noting why /effort's entry matters beyond autocomplete: set-current-as-default is the 2.14.x persistence flip surfacing on the wire. /effort and /model are session-scoped now (the disableAutoDefault{Model,Effort} settings are gone from the 2.14.2 binary — 0 string hits, set-current-as-default at 13), so saving a default is an explicit user action. kiro.dev's effort docs still claim effort persists automatically; the binary disagrees. cyril users currently have no discoverable way to save a default.
acceptance_criteria:
1. CommandInfo carries subcommands from commands/available meta (absent => empty, not an error).
2. /help output lists a command's subcommands when it advertises any.
3. Slash-command autocomplete offers subcommands after the command name plus a space.
4. Commands advertising no subcommands render exactly as today (no empty brackets or trailing separators).
5. A unit test covers the parse of a commands/available entry with and without meta.subcommands.

title: KAS host-io: bounded read for fs/read_text_file (don't load whole file when line/limit set)
description:
kas::host_io::read_text_file uses tokio::fs::read_to_string, loading the ENTIRE file into memory before slice_lines selects [line, line+limit). For a large file with a small limit (KAS's chunked-read pattern), the whole file is read and allocated regardless of how few lines were requested -- a memory spike / OOM risk proportional to file size, not request size.

Consider tokio::io::BufReader + AsyncBufReadExt: skip(start), take(limit), stop early; keep the read-whole path for the None/None case. Must preserve slice_lines' byte-exact semantics (split_inclusive keeps trailing newline; CRLF intact) and the non-UTF-8 -> Err behavior. Per-callback, not a hot loop -- low priority. Discovered during review of PR #34 (KAS-5a).
acceptance_criteria: A read with line/limit on a large file allocates ~O(requested window), not O(file size); slice byte-exactness (trailing newline, CRLF) and non-UTF-8 -> Err preserved; whole-file (None/None) behavior unchanged; existing host_io read tests still pass.

notes.content:
2026-07-01 issue-set review:
(1) Do NOT use the lines() adapter — it strips the \n AND a trailing \r, destroying the documented byte-exact/CRLF semantics. Correct idiom: manual read_line (or read_until(b'\n')) loop — delimiter included, so \r\n survives; clear a reused buffer for the `start` skipped lines, accumulate `limit` lines, break on Ok(0). O(longest line + window) memory; no meaningfully simpler idiom exists.
(2) One acceptance criterion is unachievable by construction: 'non-UTF-8 -> Err' today validates the WHOLE file (read_to_string); a bounded read cannot validate bytes it never reads. Relax to Err-for-invalid-UTF-8-within-the-read-region and document the divergence (reading to EOF just to validate defeats the issue's purpose).
(3) line-beyond-EOF still yields "" under a streaming loop — matches current behavior, no special case needed.

title: Picker never marks the active option — /model and /effort options carry no `current` field on 2.14.2
description:
cyril's picker draws its check mark from CommandOption::is_current (crates/cyril-ui/src/widgets/picker.rs:84), parsed from an option's `current` boolean (commands/mod.rs:328). Live captures at 2.14.2 show the agent never sends that field, so the mark never renders and the picker gives no indication of what is currently selected.

Captured live (v2 engine, session default model gpt-5.6-terra):

  /model  options -> keys: [description, group, label, value]        (no `current`)
          nothing marked, even though gpt-5.6-terra IS the active model
  /effort options -> keys: [label, value]                            (no `current`)
          fresh session: nothing marked
          after an in-session change: the active level rides INSIDE the label,
          e.g. {"value":"low","label":"Low  [active]"} / "None  [active]"

So there are two distinct defects:
1. No marker at all for /model, and for /effort until the user changes it once in-session.
2. When /effort does mark it, cyril renders the raw "[active]" suffix as label text instead of using its own marker.

parse_options_response's `current` handling is not wrong, just dead against current kiro-cli — the existing test asserting is_current (commands/mod.rs:745) runs on a synthetic fixture, not a live shape, which is why this went unnoticed.

Fix direction: cyril already knows both values without the wire telling it — UiState::current_model and UiState::effort (state.rs:54-58) feed the toolbar. Marking the picker row that matches cyril's own state covers both commands and both defects. Parsing the "[active]" suffix would also work for /effort but is string-sniffing a display string, and it would still leave /model unmarked. Keep the `current` parse as a fallback for agents that do send it.

Related: cyril-cc5e (Keep picker selection visible) covered scroll/selection visibility, not the active-value marker.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Opening /model marks the row matching the session's current model.
2. Opening /effort marks the row matching the session's current effort level, including on a fresh session before any in-session change.
3. A label arriving with an "[active]" suffix does not render that suffix verbatim.
4. An option list that DOES carry current: true still marks correctly (fallback preserved).
5. Render test over a picker fixture asserting exactly one marked row.

notes.content: Closed: Fixed: PR #75 (48ab05370, incl. review-findings commit 056613f). Repro: picker_marks_active_row_from_current_model + the picker_active_marker.rs render fence asserting exactly one marked row. show_picker now joins the option list against cyril's own current_model/effort; the [active] label suffix is decoded into is_current at the wire boundary; the wire current flag is preserved as a fallback.

title: KAS-2a — Walking skeleton: a plain KAS turn renders and ends
description:
The milestone that earns a demo: select KAS, authenticate, prompt, watch text + tool calls stream, turn completes, input is live again. The MINIMUM for a plain turn to render and end cleanly. Other _kiro/* surfaces (governance, mcp/status, powers, progressive_context) and the other session_info_update kinds all fire on a plain turn too, but cyril's existing unknown-variant debug! arm drops them gracefully — deferred to 2b-2d without hanging anything.

SCOPE (ROADMAP KAS-2a, docs/ROADMAP.md:165):
- Converter arm (engine-keyed, in the Engine-trait structure from KAS-0) for agent_message_chunk / agent_thought_chunk / tool_call / tool_call_update ONLY.
- session_info_update -> kind:'turn_end' mapped to cyril's turn-completion / busy-clear. THIS — not the session/prompt response — is the turn-completion signal under KAS. HANG-PROOFING: cyril's prompt-response await must be NON-BLOCKING under KAS — drive completion off turn_end, treat the prompt response as secondary/whenever-it-arrives, so a non-returning response cannot freeze the skeleton. Verify with existing probe-kas-* scripts (no new probe needed).
- Answer _kiro/terminal/shell_type ({sessionId} -> {shellType: bash|zsh|fish|powershell|sh}) — lightest host callback, called once at session setup; missing reply yields 'Shell: undefined' in the system prompt.
- Handle sess_*-prefixed session ids and per-run log dirs under ~/.kiro/logs/<ts>/.
- Defensive unknown-variant tolerance for everything else (one debug! line noting _kiro/* surfaces are intentionally dormant pre-2b).

CRITICAL REWORK (ROADMAP note, docs/ROADMAP.md:177): the off-loop busy-guard + TurnCompleted emission from PR #22 (cyril-84ca) must be reworked here. That PR emits TurnCompleted when conn.prompt().await resolves and keys the one-turn busy-guard off prompt_task.is_finished() — both encode 'prompt response == turn end', correct for v2 but FALSE for KAS (turn-end is session_info_update->turn_end; the prompt response is secondary/late). Under KAS, is_finished() stays false after a logical turn-end (next prompt wrongly rejected 'a turn is already in progress') and TurnCompleted fires late/never — the exact hang the non-blocking criterion guards against. Fix: route BOTH the busy-guard and TurnCompleted through the engine's turn-end signal (KAS-0 turn-end detection in the Engine trait), not prompt_task.is_finished()/prompt().await. Concrete code: the SendPrompt guard + spawned prompt_task in bridge.rs.

REFS: ROADMAP KAS-2a (docs/ROADMAP.md:165); existing experiments/conductor-spike/probe-kas-*.py.
acceptance_criteria:
* On the KAS engine: select KAS, authenticate, send a prompt; agent text + tool calls stream and render, the turn completes, and input becomes live again.
* Turn completion is driven by session_info_update->turn_end, NOT the session/prompt response; the prompt-response await is non-blocking (a non-returning response cannot freeze the skeleton).
* The busy-guard and TurnCompleted emission are routed through the engine turn-end signal (not prompt_task.is_finished()/prompt().await); a second prompt after a logical turn-end is accepted, not rejected with 'a turn is already in progress'.
* _kiro/terminal/shell_type is answered (no 'Shell: undefined').
* sess_*-prefixed session ids handled; unknown _kiro/* variants produce a single debug! line, no hang.
* v1/v2 engine path unchanged.

title: KAS-7 — Advertise _meta.kiro.hooks at initialize + hooks-host responders; decide the v2 standalone-loader flag
description:
Implementation ticket for ROADMAP KAS-7 (hooks host — the org write/exec-policy interception point; fully de-risked, fired end-to-end 2026-06-16 via probe-kas-hooks-host-2.7.1.py). Core work per the milestone: advertise clientCapabilities._meta.kiro.hooks at initialize (top-level KiroClientMeta key, sibling of settings — NOT an AgentSettings key; composes with cyril-nhzw's handshake plumbing); implement _kiro/hooks/list + _kiro/hooks/executeHook responders (cyril owns the hook registry from the user's .kiro/hooks/*.json and spawns runCommand hooks: USER_PROMPT env, timeout default 60s, combined output, real exitCode, abort handle for _kiro/hooks/cancel); handle _kiro/hooks/{cancel,didChange}; preToolUse executeHook exitCode 2 blocks the tool with the output as reason. Shares the host-executor layer with KAS-5 fs/terminal callbacks.

NEW since the milestone was written (wire-verified 2026-07-17, probe-kas-hook-confirm-2.13.0.py, cyril-497j): the ROADMAP's 'no v2' note is STALE — 2.13.0 KAS reads an optional v2:true key in the same hooks object. v2 activates a SECOND, agent-side hook model: KAS's own standalone .kiro/hooks/*.json loader (kasHookFileSchema, file-watched, workspace + global roots), Stop-hook confirm dialogs (_meta.kiro.hookConfirm -> requestPermission), and the CreateHookTool. With {enabled:true, v2:true} the live capture drove ZERO _kiro/hooks/* host callbacks — everything ran agent-side, i.e. v2 shifts hook ownership from cyril to KAS.

DECISION REQUIRED before implementation: which model(s) cyril enables. enabled-only = cyril as executor/audit-gate (the strategic org-policy stage; hooks cyril controls); +v2 = users' on-disk KAS hooks light up with confirm dialogs for free (cyril-497j renders them) but execution moves agent-side, outside cyril's gate. They may compose (enabled governs host callbacks, v2 the standalone loader) — probe the enabled-only and enabled+v2 combinations A/B to confirm whether both paths can coexist before choosing a default. Document the choice in the KAS wire audit + covenant doc.


--- COUPLING NOTE 2026-07-18 (from cyril-0wyn triage) ---

KAS injects its hooks system-prompt briefing (hooksBlock: createHook tool, trigger
vocabulary, exit-code semantics incl. exit-2 block) ONLY when clientInfo.name maps to
'kiro-ide' (client === "kiro-ide" ? hooksBlock : ""). The hook MACHINERY this issue
implements (_meta.kiro.hooks advertisement + host responders) is gated separately, on
the handshake. Consequence: KAS-7 cannot be designed independently of the cyril-0wyn
name decision — name='kiro-cli' means hooks run against an unbriefed model (exit-2
blocks unexplained, hook-injected context unattributed); name=cyril -> kiro-ide
fallback means the model is briefed but with IDE-only UI pointers wrong for a TUI.
Mitigation candidate either way: cyril injects its own corrected hooks briefing via
steering/context whenever hooks are configured. See cyril-0wyn TRIAGE 2026-07-18 for
the verified hooksBlock contents.
acceptance_criteria: cyril sends _meta.kiro.hooks per the decided config on the KAS engine; _kiro/hooks/list+executeHook responders implemented with cancel/didChange handling and a preToolUse-block regression test; A/B probe capture recording which callbacks fire under enabled-only vs enabled+v2; ROADMAP/audit docs updated with the decided default.
